body:
One of the ugliest voices in the New Hampshire State House, Rep. Travis Corcoran (R), took a swing at me because I told my story of being the kid of immigrants, helped deport a war criminal, but am fighting against the horrors of Trump’s ICE goons.
Who is Rep. Corcoran? He is a notorious merchant of hate. He had his guns taken away after he endorsed the shooting of Congresswoman Gabby Gifford in 2011, he proudly calls for white people to use the n-word, throws around homophobic slurs, and recently called for a jewish lawmaker to face the “final solution.” And when I got death threats by the far right, he cheered that on.
He can come at me all he wants.
I can take it.
I’m not going anywhere.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
The person I had deported was the far-right murderer of Victor Jara.
Victor Jara, was a beloved folk singer murdered by the fascist Pinochet regime. For Chileans he is what Bruce Springsteen is to Americans.
Because of his reputation as an advocate for poor Chileans and for social justice, when the Pinochet government took control in a violent coup in 1973, Jara was abducted, tortured in front of a packed soccer stadium, executed, and his body was publicly displayed as an example.
In the mid 2000s Victor Jara’s wife hired my law firm pro-bono to bring his murderer to justice. As one of the firm's only Spanish speaking lawyers I spent a year traveling to Chile tracking down leads and conducting interviews.
Ultimately we uncovered the identity of his killer and hunted him down to the US where he had become a citizen and assumed a quiet new life (built on lies) running a pizzeria outside of Orlando, Florida.
When you become a US citizen one of the questions that you must answer is have you ever tortured anyone. In court, we were able to prove he had lied about this in his naturalization process, in turn we were able to have him stripped of his citizenship and deported back to Chile to face justice for war crimes. Now he is facing justice in Chile, and should spend the rest of his life in a Chilean jail cell.
So to respond to Travis: I am proud of what I did, war criminals should absolutely be held to account and if they came here under false pretenses, they should be deported. Hardworking immigrants like my parents and the millions presently targeted by ICE (which should be dismantled) should be left to pursue the American dream.
My background and the threat I pose to MAGA (I am poised to ensure open seat NH-01 stays blue) have put a massive target on my back — the NRCC has been attacking me since day one, Nazis stormed a rally of mine, and last month leaders of New Hampshire’s far-right called for my public hanging.
We’re rolling with the punches but we need your support to keep fighting. Please can you rush a donation of $25, $10, or even just $5 to ensure a progressive fighter takes this critical seat? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
DONATE TODAY!>> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
Thank you in advance for your support at this inflection point for our campaign.
Christian Urrutia
Democrat for NH-01

“ This is not about how fast California counts ballots ,” Becker said. “ All that [Trump] cares about is whether he wins or loses. And if he loses, he’ll create a fiction in his head to tell him otherwise .”

The lies went into overdrive as the counting of California's mail ballots caused a progressive Democrat to overtake Republican former reality TV star Spencer Pratt to make the November runoff race for Los Angeles mayor.
“ The Dumocrats, right before our very eyes, are stealing the Vote ,” Trump posted in response on social media. Vice President JD Vance, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), and numerous other GOP leaders have likewise raised suspicion about the count without any proof of wrongdoing or concrete examples of problems.
This won't just bring up problems with the mail-in ballots themselves, but could also lead to a flood of post-election litigation, as opponents of voting rights, alleging fraud or the potential for it, pull out the stops to get votes thrown out and to contest results.
We have to step up and stop this election denialism and subversion before it gains a foothold. Our fundamental right to vote depends on it.

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. clean_body: | This pair is on their third set of soles, and I still wear them because it reminds me why I'm here. From me being a rookie patrol officer to being in the halls of Congress, that part of my routine hasn't changed. These boots followed me on patrol in Colorado, getting vicious gang members off the street. Now, I wear them in Congress, fighting for the victims of dangerous sanctuary state policies and having the backs of the brave men and women in blue. I served my community as a police officer for over 10 years - and I've firsthand witnessed what happens when the badge becomes the target. During the 'Defund the Police' movement in 2020-2021, Colorado Democrats turned their backs on law enforcement and empowered criminals to run the city. It came with lethal consequences. I buried one of my brothers in blue after he was assassinated by a radicalized 'Defund the Police' lunatic. I remember his locker was only five away from mine. My cop boots remind me to never surrender to the radical Democrats' anti-law and order, anti-cop, and pro-criminal agenda. I've seen how Democrats' sanctuary city policies flood peaceful communities with transnational gangs, cartels, and drug traffickers. Democrats are so focused on appeasing their Liberal mega-donors that they've destroyed families, communities, and safety. That's why my first action after being sworn in as a member of Congress in 2024 was to vote to pass the Laken Riley Act. Here's the big problem: National Democrats are already investing MILLIONS against me to flip this seat and replace me with a pro-crime, anti-cop Liberal. We won this seat by less than 2,500 votes in 2024, so I really need a rush of support to hold the line. | | Thank you for your support, Congressman Gabe Evans I've dedicated my entire life to service. From flying Black Hawk helicopters in the Middle East to serving my community as a police officer. I have and always will put serving my country and community first. Now, I'm battling Democrats in my home state of Colorado to keep this battleground seat red! This race was one of the most expensive House races in 2024 - and I won by just a couple of thousand votes. I'm grateful to Hemet's law enforcement, who was able to find the killer and arrest him.

Nicholas serves as a daily reminder to me to never take a single precious moment for granted and that I must continue to fight every single day for a better future.

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life 's mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he's determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe's entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Friend, We all deserve safe, accessible, and affordable drinking water: Water is life and we cannot live without it. But millions of our neighbors across the country can’t afford rising water bills and are facing water shutoffs. This is because over the last five years, water rates have risen by more than 24%. In Congress, I helped create and fund the Low-Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)—which provided $1.1 billion to help families access clean, affordable water. But as funding for that first-of-its-kind program ran out, Congress failed to fund it. That’s why, in response, Congresswoman Debbie Dingell and I have introduced the **_Water Access and Affordability Act_** , which establishes a new Low-Income Drinking Water Assistance Program at the EPA, funded at $20 billion per year. The average cost of water in Detroit has increased by at least 285% since the 1980s. And the EPA’s 2024 Water Affordability Needs Assessment estimates that between 12 and 19 million households lack affordable access to water—that’s up to 15% of American households! **Too many of our communities are struggling to afford increasingly expensive water bills.** That’s why we need the _Water Access and Affordability Act_ , to establish a permanent Low-income Drinking Water Assistance Program to help income-eligible households pay outstanding water and wastewater bills, avoid water disconnection, and assist with reconnection fees if service has been disconnected. ****[**Add your name as a grassroots co-sponsor of my new _Water Access and Affordability Act_ today to ensure every family has the resources they need to live with ****
When Congresswoman Debbie Dingell and I helped establish the Low-Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) in 2021, it prevented 923,583 water shutoffs, restored service to 101,687 homes, and helped reduce 1,120,417 water bills.
My whole career, I’ve worked with environmental justice advocates in my hometown of Detroit, including water warriors fighting back against water shutoffs. I promise to continue fighting for our right to clean water and air.
In Congress, I’ve passed historic amendments to provide as much as $22.5 billion to fully replace dangerous lead pipes, and successfully worked with federal agencies to protect drinking water from toxic chemicals.
I also founded and am leading the Get the Lead Out Caucus, and I just co-launched the new People’s Environmental Justice Caucus—where my colleagues and I will center frontline communities most harmed by environmental injustice, and push for policies to protect people and our planet.
****[**Water is a human right and I need your help to demand Congress act to ensure no household goes without access to clean, affordable drinking water. Thank you for taking action for our fundamental rights.
We’ll keep building movements and political power to shift our government’s priorities so we protect and invest in communities—rather than corporate profits.
With you in the fight for better,
Rashida

That’s why we need the Water Access and Affordability Act , to establish a permanent Low-income Drinking Water Assistance Program to help income-eligible households pay outstanding water and wastewater bills, avoid water disconnection, and assist with reconnection fees if service has been disconnected. ** | When Congresswoman Debbie Dingell and I helped establish the Low-Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) in 2021, it prevented 923,583 water shutoffs, restored service to 101,687 homes, and helped reduce 1,120,417 water bills. My whole career, I’ve worked with environmental justice advocates in my hometown of Detroit, including water warriors fighting back against water shutoffs. I promise to continue fighting for our right to clean water and air. In Congress, I’ve passed historic amendments to provide as much as $22.5 billion to fully replace dangerous lead pipes, and successfully worked with federal agencies to protect drinking water from toxic chemicals. I also founded and am leading the Get the Lead Out Caucus, and I just co-launched the new People’s Environmental Justice Caucus—where my colleagues and I will center frontline communities most harmed by environmental injustice, and push for policies to protect people and our planet. Thank you for taking action for our fundamental rights. We’ll keep building movements and political power to shift our government’s priorities so we protect and invest in communities—rather than corporate profits. name: Dan Osborn
subject: Why I was fired
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/113269?t=6&akid=25393%2E878179%2E4haobp) In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.

I had dropped out of college and gone to work for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.

Working at Kellogg’s used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that let you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire some day.

But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost of living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.

**So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.** [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/113269?t=7&akid=25393%2E878179%2E4haobp) Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of the winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.

After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.

It was one of the proudest moments of my life. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/113269?t=8&akid=25393%2E878179%2E4haobp) Following the strike, I was fired. Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block.

It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.

Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.

**Now, I’m running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts – and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%.**

I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat for working class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win this seat.

[Please, will you contribute to my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Voter Protection Project to help me defeat billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts here and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat? »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/113269?t=9&akid=25393%2E878179%2E4haobp) If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Dan Osborn and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/113270?t=10&akid=25393%2E878179%2E4haobp)

name: Stacy Garrity
subject: There's a place for you in this campaign
body:
Join one of our campaign coalitions to help us build a winning team across Pennsylvania.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Peter,

One of the things I've learned from traveling to all 67 counties every year is that Pennsylvania's strength comes from its people.
Every community has unique concerns. Every family has a different story. And every Pennsylvanian has something valuable to contribute.
That's why we're building coalitions across the Commonwealth to ensure that people from every walk of life have a voice in this campaign.
---
| [JOIN A COALITION](https://us.list-manage.com/BGXGsI6zFkY?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd&i=96a0ea8fe1)
---
| | | | | |
Whether you're a veteran, a small business owner, a farmer, a parent, a sportsman, a member of law enforcement, or simply someone who wants a better future for Pennsylvania, there is a place for you on Team Garrity.
Our coalitions help us:• Connect supporters with shared interests and experiences• Share important campaign updates and opportunities• Recruit volunteers and community leaders• Amplify our message throughout Pennsylvania• Ensure our campaign reflects the people we hope to serve
This campaign won't be won from a headquarters in Harrisburg.
It will be won by Pennsylvanians in communities across all 67 counties who are willing to step up and get involved.
That's where you come in.
I hope you'll take a moment today to join one or more of our campaign coalitions and help us build the grassroots movement that will carry us to victory in November.
---

# Powell to the People
---
| | | |
## Campaign Update
Nate Powell Received 3 New Endorsements
* Last week, 3 additional unions endorsed Nate:
* SEIU 775, which represents more than 60,000 long-term care workers providing quality care for seniors
* United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters (UA), representing a wide variety of piping trades including plumbers, steamfitters, HVACR technicians, welders and pipeliners
* The Sailors' Union of the Pacific (SUP), a union representing mariners and deck department workers on U.S.-flag vessels
* This week, Nate has a busy town hall schedule, continuing to meet with voters to hear their concerns.
* On Monday he was in Dayton, talking to voters of Columbia County
* Tuesday took him to Clarkston in Asotin County

body:
Ballots drop in four weeks. Now is the time to stand with Jerrod and help us hold the line. | | | |
---
| [The Rescue Washington Campaign](https://sendmanage.jerrodforcongress.com/send1/l/cRwY2WMZosKKG664LUBf1w/DSxgdne763leB9lBNPfr4hXg/R1F5M85JLJusbW7aNBPfRw "The Rescue Washington Campaign")

---
| Dear Friends,

We are working harder than ever... and somehow getting less every single year.

That frustration at the kitchen table -- bills piling up, prices rising, and the American Dream slipping further away -- is real. And it's not an accident.

In the video above, Jerrod Sessler speaks straight about what so many families are facing: homes that once took six months of salary for his parents to buy, or two years for Jerrod at age 22, require seven to ten years of salary for young families today.

This didn't happen by chance. It's the result of decades of decisions from Washington, D.C., where leaders talk about cutting spending but rarely hold the line. We now face $40 trillion in national debt while the system continues taking from working families.

**Jerrod is running to change that.**
He's not another politician who blends in -- he's fighting to bring the [Rescue Washington](https://sendmanage.jerrodforcongress.com/send1/l/cRwY2WMZosKKG664LUBf1w/sr2VuRdCoWyhEgMH2UlkoQ/R1F5M85JLJusbW7aNBPfRw) plan to Congress and be the voice that actually holds the line on spending, liberty, and the values that built our state.

With ballots arriving in just four weeks, Jerrod will be traveling across the 4th District -- meeting families, listening to concerns, and building the momentum we need to win the August primary.

**He can 't do it alone. This is a grassroots effort powered by supporters like you.**

If you're tired of the same old game and want a Congressman who will fight for your family the way he fights for his own, now is the time to stand with him.

**Will you chip in today and help us hold the line?**

Every dollar goes directly into reaching more voters before ballots drop. Together, we can send a strong, principled voice to Congress who will fight for real change instead of playing the same old game.

| | Friend,
On Friday, there were explosive reports out of Ohio. The Ohio Organizing Collaborative, a well-respected progressive voting rights organization known for an extensive voter registration operation, was raided by Trump's FBI.
The details are insane. They raided the Cleveland, Ohio office and seized computers and phones from the staff. FBI agents also fanned out across the entire state, showing up at the doors of any activist or organizer affiliated with the organization and questioning them about "voter fraud."

| Trump has now weaponized the FBI to interfere in the upcoming midterm elections.
The Ohio Organizing Collaborative is one of, if not, the largest progressive organization that registers voters in the state. They concentrate their efforts in Ohio's metropolitan areas like Columbus, Cincinnati, and Cleveland--the bluest parts of the state.
As Democrat Sherrod Brown continues to lead in the polls for Ohio's upcoming U.S. Senate election, a win that would all but ensure the chamber flips, the Trump admin is looking to put its thumbs on the scales by any means possible.
In March, it was revealed that Ohio's MAGA Secretary of State handed the state's entire voter registration list to Trump's Justice Department. That list includes 8 million people. Now the federal government has the name, address, date of birth, driver's license and partial Social Security numbers of every single one of those voters:

| Trump is sharpening his knives in Ohio. The raid of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative is just a prelude of what's to come: voter intimidation and disenfranchisement, persecution of progressive organizations and Democrat activists, and using access to voter data they shouldn't have to contest election results come November.
Democrats must fight back and save our democracy. Defend Our Courts is leading that charge. We are fighting on two fronts. First, building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. Second, building the movement to reclaim a Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.
[Free and fair elections are under an unprecedented assault by the Trump admin. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1983, [Sally Ride soared into history](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAYheGrgc0WPzbggaFSlC2dKnVEED5sWmwiILHcq6_cW-h6jvQM7-fN3GxMcZvf7Qq6hWw22GuC1qCYWOzmwaYa5w18fa4rlHvO39kwwkRHREeV8TamwwzY6wDAgGPQVCoqpRypwosm00QmCDByAWpUILwDGhxTkkxCWoajPjUiqKKE0lH03AdGJZPgRsf9MKGBgI8tl_4rx60tENKRX1D6e15x0ktrj4r4G2JXxK77vvdHfrang_M_F9vuC-LXF-KXS51_Otd9gMu4aP_YY0qxCokGMq82pj-y_avDS7PfAAAA__8uUnE_) aboard the Space Shuttle _Challenger_ , becoming the first American woman in space. ## US and Iran Sign Iran War Deal
President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian [electronically signed the 14-point agreement](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ygzAQhU8DnRj9IlyoSEPntCkZgRbYWEiMJJtxTp9RrpB2d2ff-76v-3S36DFsn_YAU9Y4Bbiyh1IgTZhscGB9xi2Ay8_jgLTE-IgTp7wntCdsmJxF_55k68wKwEG0YJgemNZasaHdzTxoDkqAcpZSLhnIm7N61rPqpRCzbdHUb7RnA6OMqb4TbuVMcw2zmoWTt0ZScFhi6r4jhrLD6t_xBalb4tF6s5dy5kZ8NHxs-HhdVxfmpVLUfZ3E5F3Dx0rT8DGXZLGQPabj-UMSxBMCeWbicS2k3pBsw1IwhkyYJGeNJNUCyQAPDBuB4EhaghWKKibaZNx5ofeYe91Iuh0W_V-18i-fL8N_AwAA__9G_ouf) to end the war on Wednesday, with Trump inking his copy at the Palace of Versailles over dinner with French President Emmanuel Macron. The deal reopens the Strait of Hormuz, lifts sanctions, and ends the naval blockade, while Iran [commits not to develop](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3CAUhZ8Gd3cE2AZvQZHG3aZNaYG5nrkJPxbg2fjtI_IK25zmSJ_Od359bp-WAqXnTxvRtCNvCb9qwNawbFRs8mhDpWdCX68Ysew5_8mb5FIBVyCWzVsK9zYN3hyIEscBjdCL0FrPYhlexglp1eQsn7XXTku38w9nuRNeTUJpNZDpNK7EIrgQs3qM_pBCS41udqOfPtjE0VPL5fE7U2ovPMKd31gee45DMK_WzsrGH0yuTK7pPnNtvWJy7WAmV95DaCbXq0L3Y3LdczwDNgQxwdmxcFXownCi3RG6NxyUbAg3FHyjDejB3dDKFU-wPlKi2optlBMUtB4a_m1ACY4rBCbXoRh_flEIVJVmE39GS-H_5vato99G_gsAAP__hQmS7Q) nuclear weapons and to dilute its enriched uranium under international supervision. Both sides have [60 days to reach](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O4yAUxfGngc4RXGywC4pt3GXbLS1sru27w0cEJFHefuR5hamP9Jd-5999uTsKlI6_LqJte14SvmvA1rAsVFzy6EKlI6GvzxixbDl_5QUE6E7oTo6LdxQ-S8-93REBFUcrzSiNMYMc-Wndtq6j08oIDZsUwkwOwBvlvAAzGc3JXjWh5SiFlIO-Kb-DNGBwHVbl-4n1Aj21XG7_M6V24h4--YXltuXIgz1be1Sm_jCYGcztxJNCuDYG85kjXiAGs_OREtVWXKOcGMzDBJMadNfKMz66y1i7S9y5oyBGTI3BzIv1jzeFQFUb1osjOvqJ8_art14WvgMAAP__xQ5-mA) a final deal. Trump said the deadline isn't hard as long as Iran cooperates, but warned he'd resume bombing if it doesn't. The full text was released yesterday. [Read the key points here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u3CAQBeCnwR0WjH_ABUUad5s2pYVh7CXhZwV4nX37K-4r3G6kkc7Rd_48tod23sXztw6o6pG2iHfxWCvmzWUdLWpf3BnRlisEzCalf2kDBjNlM-Vys9r5zzZ2Vh2IgEOHigvJhRATl91TmZkPYOQo9oFNRsIihmkCYfaFgVjk1DnV0tjMJWecT3M_2AO4AIH7tA92XMjI0Lqacv83uVifePhPemPuTQqdV89aX4UMvwisBNb7vnuzl6ZofwJrOwmsV6HNQxuIBgyp4a5A00GvaDGXqqN18aQV_1cCa5eVfd3Oe1dmQUZ2Bu38d2X90U5vBV8BAAD__61FfPc).
## DC's Reflecting Pool Turns Green
National Park Service crews spent Tuesday [pouring hydrogen peroxide](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAURb8GM7vgoaIBwSZmvemGFspT3g7wLGS6p_9-qucXJr5V99Q5_-7L3VGkfPx1CW3decn4vCLWimWh4rJHFy86MvrrMyUsG_MHLyBhaOXQqnHxjuJr6Rpvd0RA3aBVZlTGmF6NTbASVxh7o9SEe4fbaFZw2yp1r70xYKaG7PtNDmpUUql-uGm_gzJgcO1X7btJdBI9VS63_0y5Btzjix9YbhunJtpQ63kJ_UfALGCuAQPF-N4EzIETvoUEzM4nynTV4ipxFjD3EwzaQBtevvCBuT2x8Bd5bAvuEbdK-WhP5ihgbor155NipGswopNHcvTDaOqvoj0sfAcAAP__rn-BtQ) into the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool after an algae bloom turned President Trump's promised "American flag blue" renovation bright green. The bloom appeared days after a [$14.2 million project](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ8Gd7Zg_AMpKLZxl223tDAMzuyOwcIkVt5-lXsf4dbn6Oh835_7cnfElLbfbkdbY14SXidjrVgWKi4FdHzSljCcz33H4nP-lxeQMLVyapVZgiN-L0MTbEQE7Bu0ShultR6VaR429jA5vN2GwYwSxgAy9Mrp6IMzq4SpIftZk5MySio1Tl0fIigNGtdx7cNwE4PEQDWX7m-mVB8Y-Z1fWDqf94bto9bjFP0vAbOA-bquLq3-Q_HJBcxHZqrkTwFzyMlxaGt57oeAuWBk9JXS1h45c7sVxNQ63hx-d9rik-tHCdo0xYbjImY6Jy0Gue2O-OtB_ZG2l4X_AQAA___qgIKy) to resurface the pool for the nation's 250th birthday. The Interior Department blamed "residual" algae from dormant supply lines. Back in the fall of 2025, we were in Roanoke. A woman was walking by, and I introduced myself. She paused, nodded her head, and said, "I've never voted for a Democrat before, but I probably will this time." I never let that go. I always want to know why.
She explained that she had a child with significant learning disabilities, and as of the first of the year, most of the programs her child depended on were going to be cut. The school board had "reprioritized the budget," and those programs hadn't made the cut. I asked if she had talked to anyone, and she said she had. She called the school board, and they wouldn't talk to her, not even to explain what was more important than her child's education. She called the state board of education, and they told her she should call the US Department of Education, which she did.
I knew what that answer would be. There were two offices in the Education Department that should have been able to help her, and they had both been gutted...

I had been working with the great people on the Indivisible Auburn/Opelika Steering Committee. We held a "No Show Town Hall Meeting" for Mike Rogers in April, and the crowd outstripped anything we imagined. I MC'd the event and spoke about Congressman Rogers' failure to fulfill his responsibilities as the Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee.
Before I gave that speech, I was terrified. I had spent 30 years covered by the Hatch Act and wasn't allowed to participate in partisan politics. It was the first openly political speech I had ever given. The people at the event could not have been more supportive. A few even came up to me and said I should run for office. I laughed it all off.
The surprising part came next: as the protests continued, people would come up to me, shake my hand, tell me I did a great job, and ask me to run for Congress against Mike Rogers. Not run just for the sake of running for office, but specifically against Mike Rogers. Barb saw all of this, and we realized people's feelings about Mike Rogers ran pretty deep...

The Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs has appointed Andrea Searor as its first Women Veterans Coordinator, a new position created to expand outreach and support for women veterans across the state. Searor, a retired Air Force leader with 26 years of service, will work to connect women veterans with healthcare, benefits, and other resources at a time when more than 43,000 women veterans live in Alabama. State officials said the role reflects a commitment to addressing the unique needs of women veterans and improving access to services and support.

Google announced a $1.5 billion investment to expand its data center campus in Jackson County, bringing additional jobs, construction activity, and economic development to northeast Alabama. Alongside the expansion, the company pledged funding for energy affordability programs, STEM education initiatives, and local infrastructure projects, including a $2 million fund to help reduce energy costs for area residents. The announcement reflects Alabama's growing role as a hub for data center development, as major technology companies continue investing in the state's available land, energy resources, and strategic location to support increasing demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Local economic development officials are organizing a job fair in Talladega County after the sudden closure of Legacy Cabinets in Eastaboga left approximately 370 workers without jobs. Former employees say they received little warning about the shutdown and have raised questions about final paychecks, benefits, and whether the company complied with federal WARN Act notification requirements. The closure marks the second major plant shutdown in east Alabama this year, highlighting ongoing concerns about economic stability and workforce support in the region.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
Over the last few weeks, we've been out meeting our neighbors at community celebrations.
It was great to see the surprise on people's faces when they realized I wasn't there supporting the candidate, but I am the candidate. I just told them that, when elected, I will be representing every community in the district, and the best way I know to show that is to show up at their community events and spend time talking to them. For members of our marginalized communities, that really had an impact.
We had another event this weekend. It was a small gathering in Wedowee, hosted by a friend. We sat, ate burgers, and talked with people from Randolph County we had not met before. Yes, these are campaign events, and I hope everyone who met me there will vote for me, but I was also there to hear what they had to say about their community. Some of the people there are activists supporting the immigrant community in Randolph County, and the stories they told about ICE operations in the county were heartbreaking. Others were seriously concerned about cuts to Medicare and Medicaid and the impact those cuts would have on their local hospital. I'm thankful we had time to talk so I could hear what they're worried about.
If all you do is show up at an event, climb out of your air-conditioned car, take a few pictures, and then leave, you're not meeting your constituents; you're using them as a backdrop for a photo op. Getting to know our neighbors is something we have been doing for a year. I hope we get the chance to keep it up into the future.
We are 140 days away from the general election.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

## Laredo Jet Crash Kills Austin Startup Founder
A NetJets business jet carrying six people crashed onto Laredo's Loop 20 and burst into flames late Tuesday, killing [Austin tech entrepreneur Joshua Baer](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3SozAQRE8jMlHS8B8o2ITMm25IDcxg5JURJY2Nffste4_wxd3V1e_9uUwX9MHv1994ZyevNU47nzmwCKcpYGKKN5YlYd4kxcMvGLLECQy02rTa9hOhD--pLsjNhgZbsLNdb7veNAMUm2ttR_U6LENDZOaZFuq6piaCemgIBii8-4yZ1vbWmsra0rJFriw31FiaK1S1YfISUykbC78wr-Edn5zKJd6L4DaRI6vql4JRwXieZ_n3hfsnVDB-aBSMIS4YFIz4yOJ3BeMt5u2BekZO-hppRdk46bjq_42ss2CSx6Hzwjtr8py13_URcGf91aFgLJKj4_Qh-Nx2qjbXO_rwfSU_c_l08C8AAP__Wo2Lxw) and leaving five survivors. The Cessna Citation Latitude had left San Jose del Cabo, Mexico, bound for Austin before reporting mechanical trouble near Laredo International Airport, authorities said. The impact nearly sheared the jet in half and tore off its tail. As traffic stopped, drivers left their cars and ran toward the burning wreckage. [Bystander video captured by a passing motorist](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OgzAQhJ8GOiLv2hi7cHFNulx7JVrwEnxyYmRW-Xn7E3mFK0ejmdE3P5fxQimn-_WbbhzktZTxzs89swjXMVPlWH5Z5kr7KrVsaaa8SxlRoe2U7cCNkVJ-j6aNYVLRQ8sBBgeDU73Hdg3g3cALW-sGxIHUxDZ6hcZPEwAY16ZwlCkLDkBpgBMwEGvgPvYQJ02NURyTlHqSlYVftC_5XR5cT3O5tTmsItve6K8Gzw2eaTsADusQVdKcucHzJ9dtme7cfWg6H4En0_OsZ2McLqgt8qxJe-s1OWxriNsz5Zx2OzRGXW-U8mdS_nfUI-BfAAAA___9FXsr) showed people striking the cockpit glass with a sledgehammer and using a shovel to pry the door open and pull survivors free. A motorist whose car was struck and five police officers were hospitalized. Baer, 50, founded the Austin startup accelerator Capital Factory and [mentored a generation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMRp9G3hiI8m8GD1283a4dDV6JiXkhW4bEOvHbF84rdOFygAOe78_X_EUSZXv-ppVHfT_SvPGrRFblPEfKHNIPq89UFs1pF0-xaJqddR3YDnCYA0k856YK47cNd6x4xH7AfrDt3VXL2FjbY31HS9QwDe3Afed9y-xtj4OrKxkvme1wQLQ14g0ZiWvkNrQYvmsyjeUgmvJNF1Z-U3nEMx2cbz6tVRwX1b2Y-pdxk3HTdu6p6IWMmy6zcZO9DvbGTX8LXH3GTYd4lRVkg4dwPuEjhj3LQcrwwwqfaEgbLPJcXnSChABUYJUYJW0kmUHZL-A5GTdVeQz762Kl601jnytJ_Lyo_zfsMbp_AQAA__8F8o2A) of Texas entrepreneurs. The NTSB is investigating.
## Cameron County Approves Tax Break for Shipyard
Cameron County commissioners [approved a 95% property-tax break Tuesday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAQRL_GdEZeA4ZXuEhD99KmRGt7eTgxGNkbuPx9dKP8QcqRRjM658fn8okxxePrO-5k-bXm5aC7JmKmsiQsFPJPYl-wblzyGT2mynnRShupjIRpCRjTs_RNsE6FD2jIwjjBOKnhQzebDcZMBpxbwblJu3VU_WicHgyNoA2OTbTvMWVgAlAdQAsESB3QEAYIrkPRKwqRc2l5I6YX1jU9-aLS-rw3yW7MZxXdN6Fnoef7vtsLU6LH08EF07sl9PzGEnpO2WOS_4LHnUo-pM-_D36kz_sea435oFIlnmfJF8mKJR_RSya_ScaXdIXwl9BzU2w475hSrGYUvfraMf59a_j_TF5W_wkAAP__iwKL0g) to try to land Saronic Technologies' "Port Alpha" shipyard at the Port of Brownsville, a project pitched to create 10,000 jobs. Saronic, which builds [AI-driven autonomous vessels](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQRk8DGchl_gMHm5D1phuiAhdNrYxt2TVNc_tRzxUm_fTp6en9eywPZMf--RdPMvLew-Lpyo5EKC0OE9nwn2RLmA9JIfKGLktYtNJ9pfoKxsUiu3tpS2tWZScoycAwwjCqbtLlYfTeb1ZjM6gWRwtELeG-guq2hqYWp5LNB6Z6GAFUA1ADAVID1NkO7Npg0SqyLCHVcpDQG_Pu7vCiVG_hLJ05RGIumj-Fngs9X9dVn3dGj16C5_A5FXpevzJ7yrnQMybhzdFnTOHy-cXOUYVc5YPjjclWMSSp0MUDK611CzBCHY9YJmPjxc5x7oeiVc8T2f1IyO_SvYz-DgAA__-veoWe) for naval and commercial use, is weighing Brownsville against a site in Virginia. The county's incentive agreements are valued at about $211 million across four phases beginning in 2029, and would shrink if the company misses its hiring targets. The unanimous vote, with two commissioners absent, [capped a divided public hearing](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OgzAQBOCngc7INj8hhYtr6HLtlWjxbsCJwZa9geTtT9wrXP1Jo5n5uY03cN5t8zesZPh9D-NGR_bETGn0kAjDg9gmyAunEJ0FnzmMWupOyE6ofkRw_jM2JZpJ4lWVZNSlV5detlddLsbWYLFTnbS2w97qmhrZSETZQ9PWky2dOcNkp3qlZK1UpUgB1YpabBVONRSNJHQcUsULMb0h3_0n7JQqG9bSm4U55qL-KvRQ6OE4juqZ5v3EQg_nmkIPFlZKYRM2vDb-CIgxhZ2yuLaC4S2mRPAU95BETCGGTCjAiby4OL2cR7fNJzzIcpkMxsN573J3KRo5r-D8XxH-33270b8BAAD__95oiB0), as supporters touted jobs and opponents questioned the cost and the project's value to the Valley. Brownsville's Dr. Christopher Basaldu called the abatement "immoral" and urged a boycott. County Judge Eddie Treviño Jr. defended the court, saying members believed the deal was __ "in the best interest, both in the short and long term, for the residents of Cameron County."
## Texas Hosts Two World Cup Openers
Texas hosted [two World Cup openers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0TmzAMhn8NbOZs85nBQ5ds6dqRE7YAtwribCUk_74HU_duOkn33Pu8vx7jAyLFbfkJT3TymXnc8MiEIphGgoSBf6P4BHmVxHv0QFl4tNp2SnfKDGOASN-xKYObdLiZEp3pB9MPur3ZcnVd5xH6YfD9hDDD1DXBT0MAa-vW1PZWRnfCdGcGY3RtTGXQANYG29CaMNVQNBpDFE6VrCj4gTzTl9-YKs_Pktwqsuei_lHYe2Hvx3FUM3-aU-N8OFecKCj_2v-d1aUg8AezOmHqIivhAF-1c5LXAqTeWXneFlYhqZVfWXhTuC0EW7huiUEiqABEkMvkwn5Eopi7vmj08oRIV0j5v2rfzv4NAAD__2Wvkjo) on Wednesday. England beat Croatia 4-2 at Arlington's AT&T Stadium, while Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal drew 1-1 with DR Congo in Houston. Harry Kane [scored twice in Arlington](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OgzAQxfHTmM7INp8pXGxDl223RAMewCvDWPYEktuvkits_9PT0__nPt7BB3-s37Cj5edC44FXDsiMaQyQ0NEv8pwgb5wo-hlCZhqNMq1UrdT96MCH11gXzk7K3XSBVne97nrV3Eyx2aWGmzNTU02u72tV49KDxs6g6drJYFt4-x5Tre61VpXWpUYNWGlsXKPdVIGoFTrPlErekPEJeQkvOjGVM-1FsBtzzKL6EmYQZriuq1zomSMlzm8hzBD8iXIKtAozZJpnTMIMeKwBDifPLOdEwB7kxz2iA8Ys80wJJVOUMcAryyXRLtdEjyiDzBtdjq6jSNbFy4fgc9uJWq07-PD5xf-reVrzFwAA__8fQY3S)--a retaken penalty and a header--to match Gary Lineker as England's record World Cup scorer, before Jude Bellingham and Marcus Rashford put the game away. The win marked a successful World Cup debut for England manager Thomas Tuchel. For 250 years, America has been the greatest nation on Earth – not because government made us great, but because freedom did.
We became a magnet for the most talented, hardworking people in the world. We rewarded innovation. We celebrated success. We believed that if you worked hard and played by the rules, you could build a better life for yourself and your family.
That's the America I grew up believing in.
Unfortunately, there are people today who want to take us in a different direction.
The modern Left is increasingly embracing the failed ideas of socialism, government dependency, and resentment toward those who succeed. They don't want to expand opportunity – they want to redistribute it.
I reject that vision completely.
I believe Ohio can lead the nation by proving that freedom still works. That capitalism still works. That hard work should be rewarded – not punished.
[But none of that happens unless we win.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
This race is about more than one governor's office. It's about whether we continue celebrating success or start apologizing for it. Whether we lead our country toward growth and opportunity – or toward more government control and economic decline.

Nicolas Hulscher is an epidemiologist and administrator at the McCullough® Foundation with a Masters of Public Health (MPH) degree with a specialization in Epidemiology from the University of Michigan School of Public Health.
Nic plays a pivotal role in leading and managing scientific research, public communications, and policy engagement for the McCullough® Foundation. He oversees daily operations, manages all social media platforms, authors peer-reviewed publications, and presents research findings both in the media for broad audiences and at leading scientific conferences.
Since 2023, Nicolas has contributed to over 20 peer-reviewed scientific studies--including systematic reviews, original investigations, and case reports--significantly advancing the understanding of COVID-19
vaccine injury syndromes, SARS-CoV-2, H5N1 avian influenza, and the multifactorial determinants of autism spectrum disorder. For more about Nicholas and the McCullough® Foundation visit

name: Veterans for Garrity
subject: Join Stacy in Scranton on June 30
body:
RSVP today to show support for our veterans!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/WyRhfHtckh9?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,

You’re invited to join Stacy Garrity for a special **Veterans for Stacy Garrity Rally** in Scranton on **Tuesday, June 30 at 6 PM**.
Stacy will be talking about her plan to support Pennsylvania veterans, military families, and those currently serving in uniform — and we hope you’ll be there with us.
---
| [RSVP HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/e2g97enSOGO?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
---
| | | | | |
A retired Army Reserve Colonel with 30 years of military service, Stacy has spent her life serving our nation and fighting for the people of Pennsylvania. Now, she is bringing that same commitment to her campaign for Governor.
At this event, Stacy will share her vision for making Pennsylvania a place where veterans have the opportunities, resources, and support they have earned through their service.
**Veterans, active-duty service members, military families, and supporters are all encouraged to attend.** This is a veteran-centric event, but the general public is welcome as well.
Food and refreshments will be provided.
Please RSVP today to let us know you’re coming.
---
| [RSVP HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/7fCNzheu3q8?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
---
| |
And once you RSVP, please help us spread the word. Invite your friends, family, neighbors, fellow veterans, and anyone who wants to support Stacy and stand with Pennsylvania’s veterans.
They can RSVP by clicking the link above or by emailing [**rsvp@garrityforpa.com**](mailto:rsvp@garrityforpa.com?subject=6.30%20Veterans%20Event%20RSVP&body=Name%3A%0AEmail%3A%20%0ACell%3A%20%0AZIP%20Code%3A).
We hope to see you on June 30!
Thank you,
Team Garrity

I’ll keep this quick, Peter –
In the same election that Donald Trump first won the presidency, I won the Governor’s race by 10,277 votes, or 0.22%.
Now, I’m going up against his handpicked candidate in one of the races experts say will decide Senate control.
Much like in 2016, the numbers and expert ratings again seem to be in our favor – **but if we’ve learned anything from that race, we know we cannot let the polls and predictions tell us we have this in the bag.**
Grassroots support is the only reason why I won in 2016, and it’s how I plan to win this race too. So whether we capitalize on this momentum – and prove the polling right – is entirely up to folks like you.
[**Will you please make your first donation of $5, or any amount today, to help us win in North Carolina and flip the Senate blue?**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk707&amount=5&t=8&akid=1816%2E124072%2E2gfDBs)

It’s about my brooch.
#

Team,
Can I tell you a story? It has to do with this brooch:
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260618-1-b&t=1&akid=11561%2E3935704%2E7E4j57)
I grew up in Tucson, Arizona, on the edge of the Sonoran Desert. The desert covers 100,000 square miles and is unforgiving — temperatures often reach 118 degrees in peak summer.
The brooch on my dress is a silver desert rose. It’s known for its ability to bloom even in the most challenging environments. Mark gifted it to me to represent strength and determination, and I’ve worn it ever since.
The trajectory of my life changed in an instant when a gunman shot me in the head. The bullet damaged the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, leaving me with aphasia.
**The gunman tried to silence me — but like the desert rose, I persevered.**
We never know what life hands us, but what matters most is what we choose to do in the difficult moments. I chose to channel my pain into purpose.
Some days, I feel like we are fighting a similar battle for gun safety. I know sometimes the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting — or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day — I know how hard it is to keep fighting.
But we cannot give up. We cannot lose hope. Not when so many lives are on the line.
We are officially in the midterm election year, when millions of Americans will go to the polls. This will be a critical test for the gun safety movement, and our adversaries will be looking to see if we have the resources to elect gun safety champions everywhere.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. Hi, we’re worried.
In 2024, Sherrod’s Senate race here in Ohio broke the record for **most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history.** Now, this current contest looks to be no different – it could even _shatter_ that record.
Just like in 2024, outside spending groups and GOP super PACs are flooding this race with millions of dollars – bringing total attack ad spending against Sherrod to $83 million. body:
We wanted to make sure you heard

We’ve got good news and bad news. **The good stuff:** According to the latest polls, Josh Shapiro is in the lead. And Derek, that’s all because of the support and generosity of Pennsylvanians like you. **The bad news:** We’re less than two weeks out from our End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline, and we’re on track to fall thousands of dollars short if we don’t turn things around. And if that happens? We’ll have to slash our Ads Budget next month — meaning fewer Pennsylvanians hear from Josh at the same moment the far-right ramps up their attacks. # Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. and Iran sign MOU:** Masoud Pezeshkian, President of Iran, and Donald Trump, President of the United States both signed a memorandum of understanding on Wednesday evening, a fact first [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/3fc49809-a9af-405f-b5cc-6965dd19ff68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Sharif [noted](https://substack.com/redirect/0166a94a-d7d2-46b6-85a1-0f670a2b8d1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), upon confirming the signature, that the agreement "shall enter into force" immediately, and that, effective Wednesday, the Strait of Hormuz would reopen and the U.S. naval blockade would cease. Trump signed a hard copy of the agreement during a dinner with the French president at the Palace of Versailles, while Pezeshkian signed a copy in Tehran and later [shared](https://substack.com/redirect/ca13db31-7101-4952-8242-21de618eaaaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a photo of the document on his official X account, describing it as "a historic document." In an accompanying message, Pezeshkian wrote, "the Islamic Republic of Iran has always been committed to and persistent in pursuing global peace while preserving its dignity and independence." The signing came ahead of a scheduled meeting with U.S. and Iranian representatives in Switzerland on Friday, though there is conflicting information as to whether the ceremony will still proceed as planned now that the document has been signed by both sides.
* **Key provisions of the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding:**
* "The immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" as well as "ensuring the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon."
* An agreement to "negotiate and achieve the final deal in maximum 60 days extendable with mutual consent."
* A pledge by the United States to begin lifting its naval blockade immediately and "fully end the naval blockade within 30 days."
* An Iranian commitment to facilitate the safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz "with no charge for 60 days only" after which Iran can "define the future administration and maritime services" through the strait.
* A U.S. undertaking, with regional partners, to develop a reconstruction and economic development plan worth at least $300 billion for Iran.
* A commitment by Washington to "terminate all types of sanctions" against Iran.
* Iran's reaffirmation that it "shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons," while negotiations continue on uranium enrichment and other nuclear-related issues.
* U.S. waivers allowing exports of Iranian crude oil and petroleum products, alongside the release of frozen Iranian funds and assets.
* A provision stating that any final accord will be endorsed by a binding resolution of the United Nations Security Council.
* The memorandum also states that, pending a final agreement, both parties will "maintain the status quo" while negotiations continue.
* **Trump discusses the MOU at G7 meeting:** At the G7 conference in France on Wednesday, President Trump made a series of comments about Iran, the MOU, Lebanon, and the global energy market.
* Trump [called](https://substack.com/redirect/2d31b723-a3e3-4259-86c6-756892d994af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran both "primitive" and "genius," and commended its negotiating team. He also suggested that the U.S. had no right to curtail Iranian missile production. "Am I going to let Saudi Arabia have missiles, but they can't have them?" he asked. "It doesn't work that way."
* He said he [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/2d31b723-a3e3-4259-86c6-756892d994af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the memorandum to avoid a global depression, and that he was particularly motivated to avoid the fate of Herbert Hoover, the President under whom the Great Depression began in the United States.
* Regarding Lebanon, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/589c69ad-15df-419a-8040-668cc4d83c74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) peace there would require more work and that Hezbollah must be dealt with "one way or the other." He suggested Syria's new leadership would be willing to confront Hezbollah and praised Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, saying he had done "a tremendous job" and, unlike Israel, could target the group "with precision." Though he did not say, when asked, that he wanted Israel to halt its military campaign in Lebanon. "I want them to use good judgment," he said.
* Contrary to the posture he assumed during the conflict, he [indicated](https://substack.com/redirect/e42977d2-a4df-44c9-8fde-6646b2a163be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he was open to a certain level of nuclear enrichment for Iran. "It's a little hard when other people have it, other adjoining states have it, and you're not letting them have it for purposes of electricity and things like that," he said. "You have to use a little common sense."
* Trump [refused](https://substack.com/redirect/3ed4f625-6b38-4e56-821c-264544f741ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to take accountability for the attack in Minab, however, which killed upwards of 170 schoolgirls at the war's outset, saying "mistakes are made" and directing the reporter who asked him about it to his war secretary, Pete Hegseth.
* **Iran 's Ghalibaf addresses end of war, Iran's future: **Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf discussed the MOU on Wednesday at a meeting with the country's Chamber of Commerce.
* Ghalibaf [argued](https://substack.com/redirect/162097f7-91f6-45ae-a035-2cb08ad8f5d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that current negotiations with the United States differ from previous rounds, including during the JCPOA era, because they are now backed by Iran's battlefield victories. "Today the banner of victory on the battlefield stands behind the talks," he said. He also noted that Iran continued responding militarily to U.S. and Israeli actions during negotiations, saying that diplomacy must be conducted "from a position of strength." Ghalibaf also suggested that Iran would not cease to respond should Washington violate its commitments.
* The parliamentary speaker [maintained](https://substack.com/redirect/5851f87d-95a2-4fac-8be5-e812077fb1c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Strait of Hormuz would "never return to its previous condition," and that Iran possesses sovereign rights in the Strait as a consequence of its proximity. It is "natural," he argued, that it might receive payment for services provided there.
* He also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0dccbd4a-1567-4757-ad92-3dc7a85aa312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran expects access to its frozen assets through credit facilities that would place spending authority in the hands of the Central Bank, allowing it to finance imports and open letters of credit as it deems necessary.
* He also claimed that three European countries that previously [violated](https://substack.com/redirect/cb08410d-a6a5-4742-9d03-7668e7453f89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the JCPOA, pushed to blacklist Iran's Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist organization, and sought the overthrow of the Islamic Republic are now pursuing talks with Tehran aimed at lifting sanctions
* Ghalibaf, who serves as a special representative for China, also [met](https://substack.com/redirect/8f6e3fec-eb99-452e-b380-d74edad3e87e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday with members of Iran's Chamber of Commerce to discuss expanding long-term economic cooperation with Beijing, telling attendees the two countries are "true partners in every sense of the word" and that both would be present in any future regional alliance.
* **Trump defends Iran deal amid criticism:** Shortly after returning to Washington from the G7 summit early Thursday, Trump defended the MOU reached with Iran, pushing back against critics who argued the agreement did not represent a meaningful victory for the U.S. In a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/b453b22a-2ccc-4ed9-b0dc-4d87e6d6ca95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Truth Social, Trump wrote that those who believe he had not been tough enough on Iran were "either jealous, bad people, or stupid," while pointing to record highs in the stock market and falling oil prices as evidence of the deal's success.
* **Oil and LNG tankers pass through Strait of Hormuz:** Three Saudi-flagged supertankers carrying a combined six million barrels of crude oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, according to Maritime tracking data. French-flagged LNG carrier Mraikh also became the first French vessel to pass through the strait since the outbreak of the war in the region. According to tracking platform MarineTraffic, operated by data firm Kpler, the vessel departed the Gulf carrying 76,353 tonnes of liquefied natural gas, loaded at Ras Laffan Industrial City in Qatar, and was bound for Port Qasim in Pakistan.

* **Israeli drone strikes kill three, injure two on Thursday:** Three people were killed in separate Israeli drone strikes in southern Lebanon on Thursday, according to the state's National News Agency. * **Israeli military says it will maintain occupation of southern Lebanon:** The Israel military issued a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/8ac8799c-bc1c-4b96-a419-7a59f2e864d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday saying it would continue operations in southern Lebanon, publishing a map showing what it claimed were its current positions in a so-called "security zone" extending about 10 kilometers into Lebanese territory. "IDF forces have established themselves in their area of operations in southern Lebanon and continue to operate to remove threats and improve protection for residents of the north," the military said.
* **Israeli soldier killed, 7 wounded in southern Lebanon:** An Israeli reservist soldier was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/a56cbfe8-bc3c-4bcd-b837-0acab7d2dc2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and seven other troops, including senior officers, were wounded after a Hezbollah explosive device detonated in southern Lebanon on Wednesday afternoon, the Israeli military said via the Times of Israel.

* Hezbollah also fired rockets at Israeli military positions near Kfar Tebnit and Houla in southern Lebanon prompting repeated interceptor launches from Israeli forces.
* **Hezbollah 's Qassem rejects disarmament: **Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0973edaa-395d-40ae-a5da-60162f153a9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the group will not surrender its weapons under any future deal with Israel, in an address on Wednesday delivered at the shrine of his slain predecessor Hassan Nasrallah.
* Qassem demanded full implementation of the 2024 ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon, including a full Israeli withdrawal and the return of displaced residents, while rejecting direct talks with Israel as "humiliating dictates imposed under fire."
* He cast the fight as existential, pointing to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's stated ambition for a "Greater Israel" and saying "we are not fighting for a piece of land. We are defending our existence."
* Qassem also welcomed the understanding reached between Tehran and Washington, describing it as a "great victory" and a "pivotal point" for Lebanon. He thanked Iran for "linking the Lebanese arena" to the deal and "forcing Israel to stop its aggression" against Lebanon.
* **UNICEF: 247 children killed in Lebanon since March:** At least 247 children have been killed and 992 injured in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March, averaging 12 children killed or maimed each day, according to UNICEF. In a statement issued Wednesday following the announcement of a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, UNICEF's Lebanon representative, Marcoluigi Corsi, said, "We hope that this ceasefire will be indeed a real ceasefire because since the declaration of the previous one, violence against children and the conflict hasn't really stopped." Meanwhile, the UN said its peacekeeping mission, UNIFIL, has observed increased military activity in southern Lebanon, including Israeli armored movements, engineering operations, and repeated airspace violations.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and eight were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,018 killed, with 173,273 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,007 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,165, while 784 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli attacks kill two in Gaza City, wound fisherman and woman:** Two Palestinians were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/f3c2e77c-620a-4642-89bc-d51a319150d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and several others wounded on Thursday after an Israeli drone strike targeted a civilian vehicle in the Al-Rimal neighborhood west of Gaza City, according to WAFA. In a separate incident, a Palestinian fisherman sustained serious injuries after Israeli naval forces opened fire off the coast of Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza. An Israeli army gunshot also wounded a woman west of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.
* **Two Palestinians killed in Gaza Wednesday:** Two Palestinians were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/6a76e54d-d75a-44b6-b3a1-e5959b0ad42b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and several others wounded Wednesday evening when an Israeli drone struck a group of people on the beach in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, Palestinian Online reported.
* **More than 50 Palestinian Bedouin communities displaced since late 2023:** More than 50 Palestinian Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank have been [forcibly displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/d79471a2-3224-4960-927a-c4127a0e17ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since late 2023 due to Israeli settlement expansion and military restrictions, according to the results of a survey released Thursday by the Independent Commission for Human Rights (ICHR) in cooperation with the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics, and reported by Anadolu. Speaking at the launch of the survey findings, ICHR Director General Ammar Dweik stressed the need for legal protection and sustained investment to strengthen the resilience of these communities against Israeli policies, including home demolitions, land seizures, restrictions on movement, settler violence, and the erosion of livelihoods.
* **UN Chief warns settler groups could face blacklisting over violations against Palestinian children:** UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that Israeli settler groups could be added to a global blacklist for grave violations against children if the high number of abuses persists into 2026, citing a sharp rise in attacks affecting Palestinian children. The United Nations' annual Children and Armed Conflict [report](https://substack.com/redirect/b3f2d3e6-edc0-4a2a-b157-894859a81195?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) documented the killing of at least 57 children in the occupied West Bank during 2025. While Israel already appears on the report's "list of shame" for grave violations against children, the latest edition highlights settlers for the first time as a group that could be listed separately in the future. Guterres said he was "appalled" by the scale of violations against children in the occupied Palestinian territory, and expressed deep concern over a "staggering increase" in settler attacks. The report attributed 9,465 grave violations to Israeli forces and 326 to settlers.
* **Israel expands attacks on Palestinians near the "yellow line":** Israel has steadily been expanding its area of control in Gaza beyond the bounds of the October ceasefire, pushing the so-called "yellow line" demarcating its territory from 53% of the enclave to over 60%, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly ordering the army to seize 70%. Residents of Gaza City's Al-Tuffah neighborhood described tanks, gunfire, and quadcopter strikes accompanying the line's advance on June 15, forcing families to flee with what belongings they could carry. Palestinians have been subject to near-daily gunfire from newly built military bases atop 25 kilometers of earth berms overlooking displacement camps like Halawa in Jabaliya, where residents described being shot while collecting water. "No one is paying attention to us," one resident of Al-Tuffah told Drop Site. "Every day we wish for death. Every day we wish to die, to be done with this life." **Read more from Drop Site contributors Abdel Qader Sabbah and Mohamed Ahmed[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/b1f98e14-b53f-4b4b-a988-e5cbdb8bf495?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
