During an interview for Lone Star Politics, Hinojosa said she would remove Morath on her first day in office if elected in November 2026. “Well, under his leadership, I will say Texas has lost ground compared to other states. When it comes to English and reading, Texas is losing ground in the last ten years under Greg Abbott and Mike Morath,” Hinojosa said. Hinojosa, a state representative from Austin, has made education a central issue in her campaign against Republican Gov.Greg Abbott. ( ) “Texas leaders are welcoming data centers. Could it cost them in the midterms?” via ‘sBenjamin Wermund – The Democrat running for Texas agriculture commissioner won a boost from an unexpected source last week: The Republican he’s trying to replace. Sid Miller , the outgoing commissioner, appeared at a packed campaign event in Matagorda County for Clayton Tucker and told the crowd he agrees with the Democrat on many things — but especially Tucker’s calls for a statewide moratorium on data centers. “It’s not a Republican issue, it’s not a Democrat issue,” Miller told the crowd. “This is one of those red, white, and blue issues about protecting our community.” Texas is on track to be the world’s largest data center hub in just a couple of years. Most Republican state leaders, including Gov. Greg Abbott , have wholeheartedly embraced the rush as a boon for the state’s economy. ( ) “Texas Railroad Commission race pits oil field engineer against energy trader running on culture wars” via ‘s Carlos Nogueras Ramos – After a Republican primary that focused on fighting Sharia law and diversity policies, the general election for a seat on Texas’ oil and gas regulatory agency is shaping up as a partisan brawl with more talk of issues unrelated to its core functions. Bo French , a scion of the Texas GOP’s hard-right flank, is now turning his attention to a November matchup with state Rep. Jon Rosenthal , D-Houston, after French ousted incumbent Jim Wright in last month’s runoff. Rosenthal, who ran unopposed in the Democratic primary, is aiming to upset French and win a seat on the Texas Railroad Commission by touting his two decades of experience as an oil field engineer, betting he can win crossover support from voters turned off by French’s emphasis on the culture wars. French, a longtime conservative activist who recently chaired the Tarrant County GOP, and whose family runs an oil business in Midland, has said in interviews with conservative media that he’s campaigning on social issues because they resonate with his supporters. “I ran a campaign because I had to win a Republican primary,” he told right-wing podcaster Jack Posobiec on the heels of the runoff. “Talking about the Islamification of Texas, talking about DEI, talking about LGBTQ issues ... I think my victory is a testament to the grassroots folks in Texas who are tired of electing people who aren’t fighting for them on any of these issues.” ( ) “First-of-its-kind GOP midterm convention coming to Dallas in September, Paxton says” via ‘s Gabby Birenbaum – Attorney GeneralKen Paxton , speaking Monday at a tele-town hall, said the GOP will have a pre-midterm convention in Dallas this September, bringing President Donald Trump to Texas for a high-profile event ahead of the November election. The Republican National Committee has publicly discussed plans to host a first-of-its-kind gathering for a midterm election year and explored Dallas as a host site. The convention will gather GOP politicians and candidates months before the November election and place Texas — where Republican Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are locked in a competitive Senate race — at the center of the national conversation. “I know that we are having the midterm convention in Dallas in September,” Paxton said, according to CNN. “I know that we anticipate [Trump] coming to that and speaking.” The RNC, which has yet to officially announce the convention or its location, declined Tuesday to address Paxton’s comments. And the Paxton campaign declined to comment further on whether Paxton was referring to the RNC midterm convention and whether Dallas had been confirmed as the location. ( ) “Former Lt. Gov. nominee Mike Collier sues over Texas’ onerous rules for independent candidates” via ‘s Eleanor Klibanoff – Mike Collier , the two-time Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor, has filed a lawsuit seeking to overturn Texas’ system for independent candidates to get on the ballot. The federal lawsuit, filed in Austin last week, says that the bar for an independent candidate to get on the ballot is so high as to be insurmountable. “No state in the nation requires independent candidates for statewide office to gather more signatures in less time than Texas, and no other state is even close,” the lawsuit says. Collier is joined in the lawsuit by several notable political figures, including former U.S. Rep. and Dallas Mayor Steve Bartlett , former Tarrant County Judge Glen Whitley , former state Sen. Kel Seliger and Sarah Stogner , a West Texas district attorney. ( ) | STATE GOVERNMENT Editorial: “Gov. Abbott directs regulators to protect Texans in managing data center growth” via – Texas Gov. Greg Abbott took a positive first step toward an appropriate balance between modern society’s demand for data center capacity and the strain such facilities can put on local and state resources. Going forward, two key state regulators — the Public Utilities Commission and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas — and the Texas Legislature must act swiftly to implement commonsense measures. And Abbott must continue to exert his considerable authority and political influence in keeping the issue at the top of everyone’s list of priorities. Abbott issued a letter to PUC Chairman Thomas Gleeson and ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas calling for various regulatory measures to manage the unprecedented number of proposed data centers. More than 480 data centers that would be large electricity users, those consuming as much or more power as 18,750 households, have asked to connect to the grid through 2032, according to ERCOT. Abbott said in the letter that he seeks to “guarantee” that data center development “does not come at the cost of Texans and our local communities.” ( ) “Gov. Abbott issues disaster declaration for 101 counties as severe weather looms over Texas” via ‘s Amber Kite – Gov. Greg Abbott has issued a disaster declaration for 101 Texas counties as severe storms, flash flooding and excessive rainfall continue to threaten large portions of the state this week. The declaration comes as state officials ramp up emergency preparations ahead of several days of expected heavy rain and flooding concerns. Earlier Monday, Abbott directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management to activate additional emergency response resources and begin 24-hour operations at the State Emergency Operations Center. The move followed an initial wave of emergency preparations launched last week. The declaration, announced Monday, makes additional state resources available to local governments responding to ongoing weather impacts. Abbott said more counties could be added if conditions worsen. “Texas is prepared to respond to the severe weather threats that continue to move across our state,” Abbott said in a statement. “Because of the impact caused by ongoing storms and flood risks, I have issued a disaster declaration for 101 Texas counties to ensure that local officials and communities have access to the full range of state resources and support.” ( ) “Special education school voucher awards vary sharply by Texas school district” via ‘s Elizabeth Sander – For years, public school leaders, advocates and families have complained that state funding didn’t keep up with the actual needs of children with disabilities. But now, they are finding new funding gaps as Texas rolls out its private school voucher program, which offers up to $30,000 for students with disabilities. The voucher program, which follows state funding for special education in public schools, awards students in different districts very different amounts, in some cases by thousands of dollars. “None of us have ever seen anything like this,” said Andrea Chevalier , director of governmental relations for the Texas Council of Administrators of Special Education. “It’s crazy to look at the disparity between some of the districts.” Take a student who spends most of their time in a self-contained classroom and receives speech therapy. If they’re in Damon ISD, a 90-student district in Brazoria County, they would receive about $22,000 in voucher funds. But if they live in Houston ISD, the largest district in Texas with about 168,800 students, they would receive $5,500 less, according to the data. In an extreme case, Houston ISD would receive $20,000 less than Brookesmith ISD, a rural district near Waco, to pay for the most expensive placement: a residential treatment center outside the public school system. Because the voucher funding is capped at $30,000, an applicant from that rural district would receive only the maximum and not any extra funds they may be entitled to based on the state’s formula. ( ) “Austin ISD state takeover timeline and key dates” via ‘sAcacia Coronado – The Austin school district is entering a pivotal stretch that could determine whether the district remains under local control or becomes the next Texas school system taken over by the state. Three middle schools — Burnet, Webb and Dobie — are awaiting accountability results that could trigger a state-mandated intervention and set in motion a process that has already played out in Houston, Fort Worth and other districts across Texas. Without the protections district leaders sought through the state’s SB 1882 program, which provides a two-year reprieve from state accountability ratings, the three campuses now face a series of milestones that could shape Austin ISD’s future. Results to state mandated exams that are expected June 16 will provide an early indication of whether the campuses improved enough to avoid another failing rating, while final accountability ratings later this summer could determine whether the district crosses the threshold for state intervention. State takeovers of public school districts are more popular than ever across Texas. Critics argue the motivations for interventions in large, Democratic-leaning cities have political undertones. Proponents say the takeovers lead to improved academic outcomes. ( ) “Texas schools are adopting AI. What rules are in place?” via ‘s Sophia Veneziano – An Austin private school made national headlines last year for its fully artificial intelligence-powered learning model. Officials with the Alpha School have said the school uses AI to condense a day’s learning into two hours and boasted “personalized learning, done by lunch.” But AI in education has been a growing movement across the state, not just in select private schools. The Houston Independent School District announced it will launch nine AI-focused schools next year. Superintendent Mike Miles said he envisions 100 HISD campuses with AI-focused programming in the future. With a vast tech industry and a $500 billion investment in Abilene data centers, the state has become a global leader in AI. Even the Texas Education Agency uses AI to grade standardized tests. TEA began releasing spring scores from the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness exams last week. ( ) “State Board to Consider More Christianity in Classrooms” via ‘s April Towery – Are public school third graders in Texas going to be taught that Jonah spent three days and nights in the belly of a whale and lived to tell about it? That’s a real possibility, as the State Board of Education is expected to take a final vote this month on revised Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills curriculum standards for social studies. Additionally, a required reading list that includes five texts from the Bible — including the stories of David and Goliath, Jonah in the belly of the whale, and the apostle Paul’s conversion to Christianity on the Road to Damascus — is up for discussion. If the TEKS curriculum is approved, it will become effective in the 2030 school year and be in place for 10 years. A 2023 state law authorized the reading list, and if approved this month, it will be the first statewide mandatory reading index in Texas history. The increasing effort to “Christianize” public schools is concerning for Frank Strong , an English and journalism teacher who started his career in Spring Branch ISD. Strong now lives in Austin and teaches high school seniors at a charter school. His daughter just finished her freshman year at Austin ISD’s McCallum High School. ( ) | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Property tax exemptions impacting counties in Texas” via – At a March Commissioners Court meeting, David Smith , Bexar County manager, and his team revealed that the number of properties with tax exemptions increased by 50,000 since last year, resulting in less revenue for the county. “A lot more properties were able to access that exemption compared to last year,” Tanya Gaitan , Bexar County budget manager, said. “That is about $10 billion lost in property values, which is pretty significant.” Property taxes make up 80% of the county’s general fund. Gaitan said the property tax exemptions that Texas voters approved in the fall will take their toll. “The most significant one was they expanded the business personal property,” Gaitan said. The law allows Texas businesses to exempt up to $125,000 in personal property taxes annually. ( ) “More than just a fight over City Hall” via ‘s Devyani Chhetri – Dallas is bracing for a $51 million shortfall in its next annual budget, and City Hall’s fate could be tied to how the city balances its books. Lower sales tax collections, population decline and rising costs have only deepened the city’s financial stress at the same time the City Council considers costly options on what to do about City Hall. After deliberations on renovations last week, Mayor Eric Johnson called for yet another meeting Wednesday to move a step closer to relocating city services from the iconic building. Two items, if approved, will allow the city to draw federal COVID-19 pandemic relief dollars to negotiate and prepare sites to potentially house emergency and city operations. Council members Adam Bazaldua , Paula Blackmon and Cara Mendelsohn sued their own city to stop a meeting, an extraordinary step and a public sign that disagreements over city processes had metastasized. The lawsuit argued the city was trying to rush a decision on City Hall’s future. Mendelsohn withdrew her name from the suit hours before the hearing. The City Hall dispute unfolded as the mayor and City Manager Kimberly Bizor Tolbert were grappling with anxieties that downtown, the city’s economic engine, was in freefall. Recent setbacks involving moves by the Dallas Mavericks, Dallas Stars and AT&T; are boosting concerns that the region’s center has shifted away from Dallas and is moving north. They’ve also raised questions about the mayor and city manager’s ability to build support for major initiatives, including the mayor’s push to leave the government building. ( ) “Houston’s homelessness strategy faces a test. So far, the numbers are holding.” via ‘s R.A. Schuetz – The number of Houston-area people staying in shelters and living in tents, cars and other places not meant for habitation has held remarkably steady during a time of turbulence for homelessness strategy and funding. Over 2,050 people slept in shelters in the Houston region, and 1,270 were living without shelter on a single night in February, the Coalition for the Homeless in Houston and Harris County announced Friday morning. Those numbers represented less than a 1% change from the year before, despite COVID-related federal funding drying up and the unemployed population rising by more than 15,000. The fact that the numbers have stayed so similar “tells you that the system as a whole is doing what it’s supposed to do,” said Kelly Young , chief executive of the nonprofit Coalition for the Homeless, which coordinates the homeless strategy and federal grant applications for Harris, Fort Bend and Montgomery counties. That system includes the region’s longtime focus on moving chronically homeless individuals with disabilities into permanent housing and providing them with case workers, as well as a more recent strategy of directing some resources to creative, less costly interventions to people who have only been homeless for days or weeks. ( ) “Porches to penthouses: Rainey Street reflects Austin’s transformation” via ‘s Ana Gutierrez and Karina Kumar – Long before Rainey Street became known for luxury towers and nightlife, it was a small residential neighborhood sitting at the edge of Downtown Austin. Former Austin City Manager Toby Futrell says the change over the past two decades is striking. Cranes crowded the skyline, high-rises multiplied, and the neighborhood that once felt open became engulfed in downtown’s growth. Futrell, who served the city for 31 years and led it as city manager from 2002 to 2008, describes pre-boom Rainey Street as a “unicorn” — one of the last surviving Mexican American neighborhoods west of Interstate 35 as downtown development intensified around it. “It was a close, tight-knit community of color,” Futrell said. “And all around it grew downtown.” ( ) | #TXLEGE “Property tax relief among Republicans top priorities for election, legislative session” via ‘s Bethany Blankley – Property tax relief is among the top priorities of Texas Republicans heading into the next legislative session, and Gov. Greg Abbott highlighted that and other priorities that voters should support in the November election. Speaking to thousands of Republican delegates attending the Republican Party of Texas Convention over the weekend, Abbott also touted bills he’s signed into law over the last 10 years that he argues made Texas a more conservative state. Abbott called on Republicans to support two key legislative priorities next year: his five-point property tax reform plan and additional measures to fight crime. When it comes to reducing property taxes, he said, “The past few sessions, we’ve addressed priority taxes by increasing homestead exemptions, but Texans simply are not feeling the relief. As I traveled the state of Texas, I’ve talked to tens of thousands of people. Not one of them has come up to me and said, ‘Hey, governor, I’m perfectly happy with my property tax appraisal.’ And there’s a reason for it. It’s because local governments spend more and tax more and your appraisals are going through the roof. ( ) | TEXANS IN DC Matt Mackowiak guest column: “Congress shouldn’t let Brendan Sorsby’s enablers rewrite college sports” via Houston Chronicle — College athletics has become the Wild, Wild West, with seemingly little ability to self-regulate or enforce its own rules. It’s a system that desperately needs reform — but be careful which reforms you support. Never has this been clearer than the recent embarrassing saga surrounding Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who transferred from Cincinnati after receiving $5 million in Name, Image and Likeness funding, supported by a billionaire Texas Tech booster. While a college football player, Sorsby admitted he placed thousands of bets totaling nearly $100,000, including at least 40 bets on his own team, Indiana, when he was a freshman. The most important rule in sports is that you cannot wager on your own team, and you really shouldn’t be wagering at all. These rules are drilled into the heads of college athletes. So it makes sense that the governing body for college sports, the NCAA, banned Sorsby from competing for violating this obvious rule so flagrantly. End of issue, right? No. Sorsby sued in West Texas, and Judge Ken Curry of the 99th District Court in Lubbock County issued a temporary injunction allowing Sorsby to play during the 2026 season, suspending him for only the first two games. The next hearing in the matter is conveniently scheduled after the season ends. The NCAA immediately and strongly condemned the ruling, stating it “undermines and corrupts the integrity of sports.” But that doesn’t stop a judge from setting a dangerous precedent for betting on one’s own contests. Any player, coach or school that disagrees with an NCAA ruling can just sue and override it. To state the obvious: The NCAA must be able to enforce its own rules without being undermined by a local judge in a college town. The billionaire booster who enabled Sorsby’s transfer to Texas Tech and is cheerleading for his reinstatement is Cody Campbell , who has gone so far as to threaten lawsuits against anyone who attempts to punish Texas Tech. Sorsby is apparently putting an end to the entire saga by leapfrogging college football and entering the NFL supplemental draft. But Campbell hasn’t given up. He’s currently selling Congress a bill he claims will fix college sports chaos — while actively proving it won’t. This legislation, the Protect College Sports Act, opens the door to more cases like Sorsby’s by leaving intact the legal avenue that he used. Campbell’s bill deserves to be dead on arrival in the U.S. Senate. That’s because this is anything but a neutral reform effort. The bill is coming not just from Campbell, but from a coalition of billionaires and investors using Washington to rewrite rules to protect their business interests. Drafters include New York Yankees President Randy Levine and Gerry Cardinale , founder of RedBird Capital — the same firm that struck the first conference-wide private equity deal in college sports with the Big 12. Back here in Texas, we still have to deal with the fallout of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton absurdly injecting himself into the whole fight. The attorney general sent a formal letter to Big 12 CommissionerBrett Yormark threatening the conference with legal action if it sanctions Texas Tech for playing Sorsby, claiming that any sanction would be a “per se violation of federal and state antitrust laws.” Never mind that conferences can set and amend their bylaws at any time. And reportedly, that’s exactly what’s going on: The other members of the Big 12 were considering a range of options, including canceling all conference games with Texas Tech and expelling the school from the league. But Paxton’s letter — signed by the chiefs of the Texas attorney general’s office antitrust and litigation divisions — claimed any Big 12 sanction would be a “per se violation of federal and state antitrust laws.” Paxton threatened the conference by stipulating its financial exposure at “substantially more than $200 million” in lost revenue, alumni contributions, recruiting damages, and attorneys’ fees — plus separate breach-of-contract and tortious-interference claims for any altered games. His letter landed one day after Campbell teed it up on a sports podcast, calling potential boycotts “antitrust violations.” Paxton — the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas — swung the same bat for him by threatening litigation. Paxton’s lawsuit threat may be moot at this point, the contradiction remains: Campbell is asking Congress to grant the NCAA an antitrust exemption so it can enforce rules without being sued, right after wanting to use antitrust law to stop a conference from enforcing rules against him. He wants antitrust immunity when it shields his interests, and antitrust liability when it shields his quarterback. Senators should ask which Cody Campbell will show up the day after this bill passes. Campbell is selling the Protect College Sports Act as the solution to exactly this kind of chaos — but his own bill expressly preserves state contract law from federal preemption. That is the precise legal lane Sorsby’s lawyers used to win his reinstatement. The act also includes a provision to pool college sports media rights — opening the door for private equity megadeals — deals that could be structured by the same RedBird Capital that co-drafted the bill. Congress should not hand an antitrust exemption and the keys to college sports to the people actively ensuring that the bill can’t deliver what they promise. College sports need a legal framework that restores the NCAA’s ability to enforce its own rules — not a government takeover engineered by boosters and private equity investors looking for a return. The Sorsby ruling shows exactly what happens when money overrides integrity. The Protect College Sports Act puts the people responsible for that misalignment in charge of fixing it. Congress should demand better. Matt Mackowiak is president of Potomac Strategy Group, which is based in Austin and Washington, D.C. He’s a former senior advisor to three U.S. senators and a governor. “Former employee’s ethics complaint alleges age discrimination in Rep. Troy Nehls’ office” via ‘s Gabby Birenbaum — Rep.Troy Nehls is facing an age discrimination complaint from a former employee, who told the House Ethics Committee that he is one of three staffers alleged to have faced unfair treatment over their age while working for the Richmond Republican. Kevin Countie , who served as Nehls’ deputy chief of staff from 2021 to 2023, filed a complaint with the House Ethics Committee in 2023 alleging that Nehls and his chief of staff, Robert Schroeder , created a hostile work environment for older employees. Countie, hired by Nehls at age 63, said he was subject to derogatory remarks about his age and saw his job duties reassigned to younger employees before eventually being pushed out. In an interview with The Texas Tribune, Countie said he believes he was pushed out because of his age and recounted feeling insulted by age-related comments from Nehls and Schroeder. He said he raised concerns about his treatment, and about Schroeder’s conduct, directly with Nehls on multiple occasions, but nothing changed. The committee appears to be reviewing the allegation. Countie said he was interviewed by the Ethics Committee about his complaint, which was shared with the Tribune, in June 2025. The Tribune also reviewed scheduling and follow-up emails confirming the interview. In addition, an email sent last month from a lawyer with the congressional Office of Employee Advocacy — which is representing Countie in the matter — advised Countie on publicly discussing “the investigation into your Ethics complaint.” ( ) | BUSINESS NEWS “3 Texas hospitals receive $2.5M in grants for mobile stroke units” via ‘s Julianna Russ – — Three hospitals in Texas received a combined $2.5 million in grant funding toward mobile stroke units aimed at increasing access to stroke care. A stroke occurs when blood flow to an area of the brain is blocked or reduced. According to the governor’s office, mobile stroke units were ambulances equipped with CT scanners to help identify strokes and begin treatment faster. “Timely stroke care can make a life-changing difference for Texans and their families,” HHS Executive Commissioner Stephanie Muth said. Dell Seton Medical Center at The University of Texas at Austin received $1.25 million to establish a new mobile stroke unit. To expand their existing mobile stroke units, University Medical Center of El Paso was given $500,000, and Memorial Hermann Health System in Houston received $750,000. “Texas will ensure Texans across our state can access swift and practical medical care,” said Texas Governor Greg Abbott. “This $2.5 million investment into mobile stroke units will enable hospitals to better provide vital care without delay in the event of a stroke. I thank HHSC for their ongoing efforts to support our hospitals and the health of all Texans, no matter where they are.” ( ) | QUICK LINKS HOU CHRON: “Houston drone use at World Cup prompts federal charges, DPS says” American Legislative Exchange Council: “Strong Jobs Report, Texas Business Boom, and California Election Delays: Jonathan Williams on The Hugh Hewitt Show” TX TRIB: “USDA partners with DHS, researchers to kill screwworm” SAEN: “Archaeology staffers unearth second Battle of the Alamo-era cannonball” SAEN: “SpaceX unveils $60B acquisition days after going public” The Free Press: “Could a Libertarian Tip the Texas Senate Race?” KXAN: “This Texas app store law could reshape online access as Supreme Court considers challenge” TX TRIB: “Texas students saw slight gains in math, stalled progress in reading, STAAR results show” AAS: “Why the Texas GOP keeps running off its leaders” TPR: “First ‘Super’ Veterans Business Outreach Center opens in San Antonio” GovTech: “Texas Universities Fuel Semiconductor Research, Expansion” AAS: “Austin ISD takeover risk grows as STAAR scores lag at three middle schools” AAS: “Two Austin officials repaid taxpayers for meals. Now oversight is changing.” Fortune: “Two mayors, one $10 billion AI data center, and a growing divide in small-town Texas” DMN: “H-E-B set to open first namesake store in Dallas County Wednesday” DMN: “Downtown Neiman Marcus eliminating over 65 positions with closure” HOU CHRON: “The untold history of Riverside General, Houston’s first Black hospital” FWST: “Fort Worth firefighter’s funeral is this week. Wife continues search for kidney” AAS: “Emails show UT leaders’ involvement before Debbie Hiott firing” AAS: “Waymo’s Austin operations see double digit crash count in May” SAEN: “San Antonio simulation of lunar surface links city to humanity’s Mars future” DMN: “Stars CEO Brad Alberts weighs in on future of AAC amid changing North Texas landscape” FWST: “Not just for athletes: TCU’s new institute targets performance under pressure” FWST: “Koe Wetzel and Fort Worth company partner on new clothing collection” SA REPORT: “San Antonio author Dora Ramírez wins James Beard Media Award” DMN: “Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki hopeful iconic statue will move from AAC to Valley View” FWST: “Dallas Cowboys legend calls team’s business priorities a distraction (Video)” HOU CHRON: “For new UH baseball coach Will Davis, changing perception starts with winning games” | EXTRA POINTS Monday 6/15 MLB: Minnesota 4,Texas 2 MLB: Detroit 9, Houston 3 WNBA: Dallas 96, Las Vegas 66 Tuesday 6/16 MLB: Minnesota 12,Texas 2 MLB: Houston 4, Detroit 2 Wednesday 6/17 MLB: Houston 4, Detroit 2 WNBA: Golden State 91, Dallas 80 Tonight’s Texas sports schedule: 1:35pm: MLB: Minnesota at Texas Tomorrow’s Texas sports schedule: 2pm: WORLD CUP: USA vs. Australia (Fox) 7:05pm: MLB: San Diego at Texas 7:10pm: MLB: Cleveland at Houston | TEXAS SPORTS HEADLINES / LINKS TEXAS RANGERS: “Rangers headed for rotating cast in center field with Evan Carter, Michael Helman out” TEXAS TECH FOOTBALL : “Brendan Sorsby plans July workout for NFL teams before supplemental draft, AP source says” TEXAS ATHLETICS : “How the Texas Longhorns won Director’s Cup as nation’s best athletic program“ AUSTIN FC** : “3 things to know about new Austin FC coach Jim Curtin” _ | | | | Update your email preferences or unsubscribe (C) 2026 Must Read Texas 228 Park Ave S, #29976, New York, New York 10003, United States |

# _Our Weekly Newsletter Is Here!_
---
| |
## _Early Voting Opens TODAY!_
---
| | **Today is the day we've been working toward for months: Early Voting is officially open!****Elizabeth and her team are incredibly honored to have made it to this incredible point, and we're so proud of everything this campaign has accomplished to get here. Every conversation, every door knocked, every volunteer shift, and every supporter who has joined us along the way has helped make this moment possible.****Now it's time to vote.****Make a plan, double-check your voting information, and bring a friend along! Voting is one of the most important things we do as citizens, so make it fun and make it count.****Every vote truly does count. In a primary election, turnout matters because voters have the opportunity to choose the candidate they genuinely connect with, the person they believe will best represent their values and priorities. Your voice matters, and your vote can make all the difference. Let’s get out there, Virginia!****This past week, Elizabeth was honored to speak at a local Pride event, which coincided with the anniversary of the Pulse Nightclub shooting. For Elizabeth, it was a meaningful moment of reflection. At the time of the tragedy, she was deployed in Africa serving our country. And after watching the nation grieve from overseas, her belief in building communities where everyone feels safe and valued was reinforced. ****Elizabeth has also thoroughly enjoyed participating in candidate forums across the district. These events have provided wonderful opportunities to share her vision, answer voters' questions, and connect directly with members of the community. Hearing from engaged voters and discussing the issues that matter most continues to be one of the most rewarding parts of this campaign. ****As the polls open, we want to take a moment to say thank you. To everyone who has supported this campaign, thank you for everything you have done to make this dream a reality. We are so grateful for you, and we’re excited to keep this campaign rolling.**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Upcoming Events:**
**We’ve got another busy week ahead of us! First things first, please get out to the polls! Elizabeth made a voter guide, and you can access it**[**here**](https://elizabethforvirginia.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7568ef2270fb76d1ad97da0de&id=f34ce5c493&e=2f83c585b2)**. On Thursday evening, Elizabeth will be joining the **[**Henrico Dems Summer Social.**](https://us.list-manage.com/7HB0lA0KpN2?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**Join us for some ice cream, conversation, and a fun summer evening. As usual, we will be hosting**[**phonebanks**](https://us.list-manage.com/TXcRjf2BUca?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**every week on Tuesday, Thursday, and Sunday. On Saturday, Elizabeth will be celebrating**[**Juneteenth in King William.**](https://us.list-manage.com/HF_UWigeF8q?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** Come join us for the celebration! Afterwards, we’ve got more ice cream - join Elizabeth and the team at the **[**Middle Peninsula Ice Cream Social**](https://us.list-manage.com/Ijcv8t8tRpU?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** on Saturday afternoon. ****Then, on Saturday evening, we’re joining the**[**Bookshelf on Church for their Pride Party.**](https://us.list-manage.com/4i0NmFyoyU9?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**Come out for a fun night of raffles, food, and prizes. Sunday brings the campaign to a**[**canvass in Chesterfield**](https://us.list-manage.com/95xxWghZoUH?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**\- let’s go knock doors and talk to voters!****Have a great rest of your week, Virginia!**

name: Kevin Ford Jr.
subject: I’m Proud to Endorse Kevin Ford as My Successor
body:
I Believe Kevin Ford Is That Leader Made.
| [ ](https://kfj4md.com/l/TVoGOHIdjYFP)
---
Friend,

After decades of serving the people of District 24 and Prince George's County, I have made an important decision about the future of our community. [I am proud to endorse Kevin Ford, Jr. as my successor in the Maryland State Senate. ](https://kfj4md.com/l/99bRbm7N8Egc) [](https://kfj4md.com/l/kEbCX5u0f1vb) Throughout my career, I have always taken seriously the responsibility of supporting leaders who are prepared to serve our community with integrity, commitment, and results. Before I support anyone, I do my homework.

I have had the opportunity to sit down with Kevin, meet his family, and learn about their long history of giving back to our community. I have seen firsthand his commitment to service, his passion for helping others, and his vision for the future of District 24.

As I have said before:

_"I don't support people because I like them. I support people who can get the job done. The needs of the 24th Legislative District are too important, and we need leadership that is ready, willing, and able to deliver for our children, our seniors, and our families. I believe Kevin Ford is that leader."_

Our district faces important challenges and tremendous opportunities. We need leadership that understands our community, values our families, and is prepared to fight for the resources and investments our residents deserve.

Kevin has demonstrated a commitment to service that reflects the values we share in District 24. He understands the importance of strong schools, safe communities, economic opportunity, and ensuring that families have the support they need to succeed.

As I prepare to retire from the Maryland State Senate, I do so with confidence that District 24's future is bright. I believe Kevin Ford, Jr. has the experience, character, and dedication necessary to continue moving our community forward.

[I ask you to join me in supporting Kevin Ford, Jr. for Maryland State Senate. ](https://kfj4md.com/l/9HEK2umuWdBe) Grateful for you,

Sen. Joanne C. Benson

Maryland State Senate

District 24

Friend, The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge is truly one of the last wild places left in America and one of the most critical for wildlife and Indigenous communities — and a reminder of what we stand to lose if we fail to protect our public lands. And it’s in Donald Trump’s destructive path. His administration has been trying to sell off parts of this irreplaceable refuge for oil and gas drilling, and I’m fighting back. **[Will you join me in protecting the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge? Add your name to fight the destruction of one of our country’s most cherished public lands.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133572437/628333328/1206396268?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260618_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNDZkYThkOC0yZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=okkYQyTpp34w6hUU7NPVFM0o1pgMW2v6_FQx90ZJazo=&emci=a0edc2de-786a-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=046da8d8-2e6b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=252045)** | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133572438/628333331/1206396268?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260618_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNDZkYThkOC0yZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=okkYQyTpp34w6hUU7NPVFM0o1pgMW2v6_FQx90ZJazo=&emci=a0edc2de-786a-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=046da8d8-2e6b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=252045)

Our public lands are not bargaining chips to pay for billionaire tax breaks. They belong to all of us — not to Donald Trump. He’s trying to sell off this vital public asset to the highest bidder just because he can. Never mind that major oil companies have walked away from Arctic Refuge drilling, and major banks have refused to finance it. Previous lease sales have generated little to no industry interest.
_But Trump keeps pushing forward, ignoring the environmental risks, the concerns of Indigenous communities, and all of the public opposition._
The Arctic Refuge provides critical habitat for migratory birds and caribou that many Alaska Native communities depend upon. It also has deep cultural and spiritual significance for Indigenous peoples.
**Once it’s damaged, we can’t simply put it back together. That’s why I’m fighting back and asking you to stand with me.** Together, we can send a clear message: America’s most treasured public lands are **_not_** for sale.
**[Friend, will you add your name to our petition demanding that the Trump administration stop its attacks on the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and protect America’s public lands for future generations?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133572439/628333333/1206396268?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260618_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNDZkYThkOC0yZTZiLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=okkYQyTpp34w6hUU7NPVFM0o1pgMW2v6_FQx90ZJazo=&emci=a0edc2de-786a-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=046da8d8-2e6b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=252045)**

subject: Trump’s ‘philosophy’ is simple: Gimme money!
body:
He isn’t trying to change the world – he’s trying to fill his pockets

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133575766/628344286/2130526953?refcode=emwrapper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDFlNTJjMWQtMzI2Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WOqLyRmjJLU9i3ZXwvh8HGWVKtXpj4k51atI08soees=&emci=c8e52c1d-326b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&emdi=d1e52c1d-326b-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=14016711)
Hi — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.
Political commentators often tie themselves in knots trying to explain Donald Trump’s worldview.
Is he an isolationist? A nationalist? An heir to Andrew Jackson? Does he have some larger vision for America?
I think the answer is much simpler.
In this piece, I argue that Trump isn’t guided by a coherent political philosophy at all. More often than not, his actions make sense when viewed through a different lens: personal profit, personal power, and personal gratification.
[**Before you read on, I hope you'll consider supporting COURIER. Independent journalism matters because powerful people benefit when the media overcomplicate what’s right in front of us.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133575767/628344287/90330534?refcode=20260617_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDFlNTJjMWQtMzI2Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WOqLyRmjJLU9i3ZXwvh8HGWVKtXpj4k51atI08soees=)

Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133575768/628344288/90330534?refcode=20260617_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDFlNTJjMWQtMzI2Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WOqLyRmjJLU9i3ZXwvh8HGWVKtXpj4k51atI08soees=)
Donald Trump is not a philosopher king. He’s a mob boss.
He’s not even doing politics. He’s running big-bucks scams by political means.
I feel the need to clarify this because some people insist on pretending there’s some overarching ideological bent to Trump’s behavior, that “America First” is a real doctrine, that Trump is the reincarnation of James Monroe or Andrew Jackson.
Trump’s motivations came up in an NPR interview last January. Host Scott Detrow asked Atlantic reporter Ashley Parker an embarrassingly naive question: “Do you have a sense of what you think Trump’s end goals are? Is it, I want to tear down democratic norms, or is it something more straightforward of, I want to be a notable, famous president, or is it even more moment to moment and topic to topic than that?”
Sure, Scott. Trump just wants to be “notable.”
[DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133575769/628344289/90330534?refcode=20260617_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDFlNTJjMWQtMzI2Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WOqLyRmjJLU9i3ZXwvh8HGWVKtXpj4k51atI08soees=)
Parker answered: “I don’t think he has a particular pointed desire to tear down democratic norms ... He wants to do what he wants to do unconstrained by laws and norms in the Constitution.”
Kind of a weird answer. I think she meant Trump doesn’t have a political philosophy. But he does have a one-word personal philosophy: “Gimme.”
Trump doesn’t believe in anything other than indulging his predatory appetite in all things, especially concerning money but also when it comes to the abuse of women.
One of the biggest issues he ran on in 2024 was avoiding foreign wars, yet now he’s desperately trying now to escape from a war of his own choice with Iran.
He’s long talked about balancing the budget, but he runs huge deficits.
[DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133575770/628344290/90330534?refcode=20260617_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDFlNTJjMWQtMzI2Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WOqLyRmjJLU9i3ZXwvh8HGWVKtXpj4k51atI08soees=)
He’s successfully exploited the immigration issue, spreading hatred about newcomers to this country, even though he married two of them. But even then, he’s making an exception for white Afrikaners from South Africa in an attempt to please racists like Elon Musk.
To Trump, issues are tools to attract donations, win votes, and amass power – not to benefit the public. Here’s what he really cares about:
* Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche unilaterally gave Trump and his family immunity from tax investigations. That’s outright theft from the U.S. Treasury while people like us pay our taxes.
* Trump urged the public to buy Dell computers, and the Pentagon gave the company a $9.7 billion contract. We later learned that before those actions, Trump bought at least $1 million in Dell stock.
* Trump reduced threatened tariffs on imports from Vietnam after the country fast-tracked a $1.5 billion Trump Organization resort there.
* Changpeng Zhao, the billionaire founder of Binance, helped out a Trump family business and got a Trump pardon in a money-laundering case.
* Trump approved the sale of American AI chip technology to the United Arab Emirates after a UAE sheik secretly bought 49% of a Trump crypto business.

I could go on and on with examples like this, but you get the idea.
For Trump, control over the U.S. government is not an opportunity to shape a nation’s destiny. It’s a way for him to cash in on his power. And he’s certainly done that, with profiteering that netted him and his family $4 billion in the first year of his second term, according to the New Yorker.
If Trump cares about anything other than money, it’s not the public welfare – it’s his pet projects to build European-style throwback monuments and splash gold paint on things. That’s not a philosophy or even an aesthetic. It’s an unhinged old guy playing with toys.
Yet despite the obvious grifting and bizarre distractions, Trump backers still pretend there’s an overarching vision.
Over the weekend, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used the stupid phrase “Donroe Doctrine” to cast U.S. military aggression in the Americas as a well-thought-out strategy. The Monroe Doctrine, of course, warned European powers to stay out of the affairs of the Western Hemisphere. Hegseth said the new Donroe Doctrine, in which the Trump regime bullies its neighbors and steals Venezuela’s oil, is “an incredible reinforcement of the Monroe Doctrine.”
But it’s not a philosophy. It’s just a smash-and-grab.
Meanwhile, University of Florida professor Walter Russell Mead has compared Trump to a different president, Andrew Jackson, citing the MAGA leader’s “ideological, rhetorical, and cultural links to the Jacksonian tradition in American life.”
I suppose there are similarities. They both abused their power, uprooted people from their homes, and showed disdain for the courts. But it’s not a shared philosophy – it’s just (in the words of Ashley Parker) that “he wants to do what he wants to do.”
To me, Trump is best described with the words of the 20th century Chicago philosopher Al Capone:

“A crook is a crook, and there’s something healthy about his frankness in the matter. But any guy who pretends he is enforcing the law and steals on his authority is a swell snake. The worst type of these punks is the big politician.”

Is it, I want to tear down democratic norms, or is it something more straightforward of, I want to be a notable, famous president, or is it even more moment to moment and topic to topic than that?” Sure, Scott. Trump just wants to be “notable.” = Parker answered: “I don’t think he has a particular pointed desire to tear down democratic norms ... He wants to do what he wants to do unconstrained by laws and norms in the Constitution.” Kind of a weird answer. I think she meant Trump doesn’t have a political philosophy. But he does have a one-word personal philosophy: “Gimme.” Trump doesn’t believe in anything other than indulging his predatory appetite in all things, especially concerning money but also when it comes to the abuse of women. One of the biggest issues he ran on in 2024 was avoiding foreign wars, yet now he’s desperately trying now to escape from a war of his own choice with Iran. He’s long talked about balancing the budget, but he runs huge deficits. = He’s successfully exploited the immigration issue, spreading hatred about newcomers to this country, even though he married two of them. But even then, he’s making an exception for white Afrikaners from South Africa in an attempt to please racists like Elon Musk. To Trump, issues are tools to attract donations, win votes, and amass power – not to benefit the public. Here’s what he really cares about: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche unilaterally gave Trump and his family immunity from tax investigations. That’s outright theft from the U.S. Treasury while people like us pay our taxes. Trump urged the public to buy Dell computers, and the Pentagon gave the company a $9.7 billion contract. We later learned that before those actions, Trump bought at least $1 million in Dell stock. Trump reduced threatened tariffs on imports from Vietnam after the country fast-tracked a $1.5 billion Trump Organization resort there. Changpeng Zhao, the billionaire founder of Binance, helped out a Trump family business and got a Trump pardon in a money-laundering case. Trump approved the sale of American AI chip technology to the United Arab Emirates after a UAE sheik secretly bought 49% of a Trump crypto business. I could go on and on with examples like this, but you get the idea. For Trump, control over the U.S. government is not an opportunity to shape a nation’s destiny. It’s a way for him to cash in on his power. And he’s certainly done that, with profiteering that netted him and his family $4 billion in the first year of his second term, according to the New Yorker. If Trump cares about anything other than money, it’s not the public welfare – it’s his pet projects to build European-style throwback monuments and splash gold paint on things. That’s not a philosophy or even an aesthetic. It’s an unhinged old guy playing with toys. Yet despite the obvious grifting and bizarre distractions, Trump backers still pretend there’s an overarching vision. Over the weekend, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used the stupid phrase “Donroe Doctrine” to cast U.S. military aggression in the Americas as a well-thought-out strategy. The Monroe Doctrine, of course, warned European powers to stay out of the affairs of the Western Hemisphere. Hegseth said the new Donroe Doctrine, in which the Trump regime bullies its neighbors and steals Venezuela’s oil, is “an incredible reinforcement of the Monroe Doctrine.” But it’s not a philosophy. It’s just a smash-and-grab. Meanwhile, University of Florida professor Walter Russell Mead has compared Trump to a different president, Andrew Jackson, citing the MAGA leader’s “ideological, rhetorical, and cultural links to the Jacksonian tradition in American life.” I suppose there are similarities. They both abused their power, uprooted people from their homes, and showed disdain for the courts. But it’s not a shared philosophy – it’s just (in the words of Ashley Parker) that “he wants to do what he wants to do.” To me, Trump is best described with the words of the 20th century Chicago philosopher Al Capone: “A crook is a crook, and there’s something healthy about his frankness in the matter. But any guy who pretends he is enforcing the law and steals on his authority is a swell snake. The worst type of these punks is the big politician.” = Email us: mailto:info@couriernewsroom.com =

Cliff Schecter sits down with investigators Kait Justice of Downwind of Truth and Ellie Leonard for an off-schedule Epstein Update that connects the dots most newsrooms won't touch.
They open on the story that should embarrass every editor in America: the report that New York Times stars Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan sat on Situation Room audio--J. D. Vance and company workshopping how to use Ghislaine Maxwell to clear Donald Trump--long enough to package it into a book deal, while the survivors who have spent years begging to be heard got nothing.
From there, Kait walks through the financial machinery hiding in plain sight: the stablecoin grift behind Trump's World Liberty Financial, Howard Lutnick's family stake in Tether, the GENIUS Act author who jumped straight from the White House to a crypto CEO chair, and the Epstein emails that read like a blueprint for the whole scheme.

The conversation widens into the argument that ties Blue Amp Media together: this is the predator class, and the same men who preyed on children prey on your wages, your health care, and your democracy. Cliff and the team do the math on what taxing ten billionaires could actually buy--universal child care, free public college, paid family leave--and why none of it happens. It's furious, funny, and fully sourced. Watch the whole thing.

Peter, JD Vance went on The View this week, and it didn’t go well for him...

JD just wanted to talk about his new book, but instead, he was grilled on the Trump administration’s failure to lower prices, reluctance to release the Epstein files, and how he could go from calling Trump “America’s Hitler” to “America’s best hope.”
**The hosts asked him hard-hitting questions and didn’t let him off the hook when he made excuses and tried giving word salad answers.**
When they pointed out that Trump has called the country’s affordability crisis “a hoax” while spending millions of taxpayer dollars on vanity projects like a ballroom, a UFC cage match, and painting the reflecting pool, JD claimed he meant it’s a hoax that Republicans caused the worsening inflation and rising costs hurting Americans.
One host pointed out, “He just said he loves the inflation!” After JD once again tried to spin what Trump actually said, he was met with pushback:
**“That’s not what he said.” “Are you his interpreter, or are you the Vice President?”**
It goes to show just how out of touch JD, Trump, and MAGA Republicans are with the working families of this country struggling to get by.
_He was right about one thing, though:_ **The American people will make their verdict at the ballot box in November.**

| MassGOP Blasts Beacon Hill Insiders and Governor Healey for Blocking Voters' Chance to Lower the State Income Tax BOSTON -- The Massachusetts Republican Party expressed outrage that a process controlled by a supermajority of insiders has once again denied Massachusetts voters the opportunity to decide on a voter-initiated question. The Supreme Judicial Court's ruling disqualifying the ballot question, due to technical issues with Attorney General Andrea Campbell's summary, is the latest example of one-party rule in Massachusetts protecting the status quo at the expense of working families. "This is what unchecked power looks like," said a MassGOP Amy Carnevale, Chairwoman of the Massachusetts Republican Party. She continued, "Governor Healey, Attorney General Campbell, and party insiders would rather silence voters and protect the tax-and-spend status quo than trust the people of Massachusetts to decide their own future. While families struggle with skyrocketing costs, Beacon Hill Democrats celebrate by telling voters they have no right to decide how much they are taxed. Beacon Hill Democrats are acting like its 1775 all over again and they are the British." More than 100,000 Massachusetts residents signed petitions in support of the measure to lower taxes, and it was recently supported by 65% of voters in a Boston Globe/Suffolk University poll. Carnevale concluded, "Yet, once again, the voices of taxpayers are being ignored in favor of special interests and party insiders. The Healey administration's late objections only confirm what Massachusetts families already know: relief from the increasingly crushing financial burden of living in Massachusetts is not a priority for those in power." The Massachusetts Republican Party will continue to fight for lower taxes, fiscal responsibility, and real solutions to make Massachusetts affordable and competitive again.
###

name: Claire Valdez
subject: ICE was never meant to protect us
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In NY-7, roughly one in three of our neighbors was born outside this
country. Many more came here from somewhere else in search of work,
safety, or a better life. This district, our district, is living proof
that solidarity and diversity make us stronger.

ICE is designed to destroy exactly that.

Not just through mass deportations, but through fear. Through workplace
raids that terrorize entire industries. They show up seemingly at random,
making people afraid to send their kids to school, go to the doctor, or
call the police when they have been hurt. ICE does not just remove people.
It oppresses whole communities.

I have stood alongside immigrant coworkers, watched them organize for
dignity on the job, and seen how the threat of deportation is used to keep
wages low and workers silent. ICE is a tool of the bosses as much as it is
a tool of white nationalists. The two have always gone together.

That is why I am not calling for reform. I am calling for abolition.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260618-1-cv.Q4lMyV&refcode=em20260618-37921&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37921%2E1203867%2EvDZREV ]STAND UP AGAINST ICE

In Congress, I will fight to dismantle ICE, legalize the status of
millions of immigrant Americans, and build an immigration system rooted in
human dignity, not enforcement for enforcement’s sake.

But here is what I need you to understand: the forces defending ICE have
unlimited money. What we have is each other.

This campaign does not take corporate PAC money. We do not have hedge fund
bundlers or real estate developers writing big checks. What we have is a

Democratic operatives recruited an oyster farmer, got him funded, and packaged him as a grassroots movement with no organic roots.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/80872dbf-17ed-470d-ad42-dc3a51675dec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In late July 2025, two organizers knocked on a door in Sullivan, Maine.[ Daniel Moraff and Leanne Fan](https://substack.com/redirect/c0395381-d9d8-4940-ab13-66eb77774b5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a couple tied to the Democratic Socialists of America, had gone looking for a candidate to run against Senator Susan Collins.
Behind the door stood Graham Platner, a forty-one-year-old oyster farmer and combat veteran who had never run for anything larger than town harbormaster. Within three months Platner had a[ Bernie Sanders endorsement](https://substack.com/redirect/d5fe517f-aae8-4017-a58b-bbb3e8621f28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a launch video cut by the strategist who built Zohran Mamdani's mayoral campaign, and a fundraising haul large enough to push a sitting governor out of the race.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9156c213-3e06-4470-aa16-2906fe97e74e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Senator Bernie Sanders
There is a lot of speculation about Graham Platner online. So much so that [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/redirect/87dd823a-b0c4-48f4-8ef2-135424f49cb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) decided to gather the facts so voters know exactly who Graham Platner is, where he came from, what he believes, and why the current controversies have spread like wildfire online.
**The goal is simple:** cut through the rumors, strip away the party spin, and give Democratic voters the facts they need to judge the people asking for their trust
_[Find Our Mission Here](https://substack.com/redirect/32486280-ad85-446c-b92d-03ba38cf0be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
* * *
### Where He Came From
Graham Cunningham Platner was[ born September 1, 1984, in Blue Hill, Maine](https://substack.com/redirect/e9923c22-9dc8-436e-9ba4-b4abcf9ed686?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and raised in the coastal towns of Sullivan and Ellsworth. His mother, Leslie Harlow, ran restaurants and small businesses over the years, among them a wreath operation, a coffee shop, and a smoked salmon company.
His father, Bronson Platner, worked as an Ivy League educated attorney. Both parents gave money to Democratic candidates. They separated when Graham was six. His grandfather,[ the modernist architect Warren Platner](https://substack.com/redirect/8f6592a0-3e4f-4022-a186-a92a08d02466?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), designed interiors for the Ford Foundation and for Windows on the World, the restaurant atop the original World Trade Center. The family had money and an ivy league pedigree long before Graham found the oyster boat...

Secretary Mullin just laid out the horrific fate of 450,000 children

| | | | | |

[ ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=620e97c4c57c4646b6b9f9f40681f2ad&_e=xpSgMQfa-41NlR4WaoX9yA5KH2M9RrK0IrF-xQ9qz8kZKaciB2C7vjxsI0t3ufMPfBhX2DKFl5PvZTu5GQNCqxcstybUNyJMlHWf-TzzDYGAPI0lfvb-0hLY6cSIuqFpFBWjJr7rclwW0xLG9eSgPNNgG5YfPPhmXc-ItHvVUU4kRh4Cj4ePJkc1ITyGR9cuD569DJ3PDlWFig8_RghWM_CX--sDKemeyDK7EIyDQTmuLuFAK8iVKVcEd6_8xG_NNjcccmtCgyxtSXCdYI8JZMhPI7NgcTDSvYD8eNwsu2uReTgz1Zbv_z69ZDu7PzjYqTtx_o2ik-FKss07Zi-RYAvBMIAphOfY2QirQHX98zZS-6VLUXUqRMMR13UZHP9x38ldfOYcXwi1m7Ubg5iO7gLQpY7YdtnYO8pXK3Y5HbpkWx2TwoQm1VEigzoB_uc-r5KBoUBsm1r0zYP5pwdjX_B1eS19WzIyiIZ0q3_Qbu5d4nfbvwOxvLXNItTXjcy48jcePooTpkZ83FH1zaefNpX0MXz5N6ZL-BW9E7LnvbrXF3dg0KzZ6w22rdhQTeNG7jjfOmNTjapnGOgkMnMjiV_EQLn2mwy-JpBxB5k0TAEr86sjDlELqL6ANhT9Ymch5uLu-zF1j2tNJMl8DG3d8hU_MKnZNis_mptgkIkiv2UDXQ02eF33NGNq-sCo1aaP28Ho4_PsWerYdtzHyywY1Q%3D%3D)
---
Peter,
Flanked by the Acting Attorney General at DOJ headquarters, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin just stood before cameras, stone-faced but emotional, and said it plainly:
_**"As a father of six, three of them young girls, I’ll do whatever it takes. I’ll move heaven and hell to go find these kids.”** _
He laid out in horrific detail the tragic fate of **at least 450,000 children** – from their journey to our previously broken border to their transfer to unvetted sponsors.
Over a third of the females, regardless of age, were reportedly sexually assaulted before they even reached the border.
And once here, **65,605 reports of abuse and neglect were filed and left to sit** – among them, 7,346 reports of human trafficking. __**Ignored.** _ _
Some of these children reported being raped **over 600 times.**
"Neglect at best, criminal at worst," as Secretary Mullin called it.
**146,000 have been located so far, but hundreds of thousands are still unaccounted for.**
These are not statistics – _they are children_.
I don't share this to politicize things, or to paralyze you. I share it because it demands a response.
My name is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine special operator with over 19 years of service and 15 overseas deployments both in the military and private contracting, and I’m writing to you today as Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity.
**We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Today we are a 501(c)(3) network of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals and everyday people committed to being the hands and feet of Jesus Christ.**
Since 2026 began, we have conducted **anti-trafficking operations across 11 states** and as you read this, we’re deployed – boots on the ground – working as a quick reaction force alongside trusted local partners for the World Cup – a magnet for trafficking the scale of which we’ve never seen. **Already we’ve rescued 14 trafficking victims leading to multiple arrests.**
The skills that made our operators effective in combat overseas – surveillance, network mapping, moving through hostile environments, finding people who do not want to be found – are exactly the skills we’re now putting to use to find vulnerable young women and children.
**We know how to find them and bring them home –** _**but we need your prayers and support.** _
[ **Your tax-deductible contribution today directly funds our operators in the field – the training, the mobility, the intelligence work, the equipment, the ability to move fast when a lead goes live.** ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=620e97c4c57c4646b6b9f9f40681f2ad&_e=xpSgMQfa-41NlR4WaoX9yA5KH2M9RrK0IrF-xQ9qz8kZKaciB2C7vjxsI0t3ufMPfBhX2DKFl5PvZTu5GQNCqxcstybUNyJMlHWf-TzzDYGAPI0lfvb-0hLY6cSIuqFpFBWjJr7rclwW0xLG9eSgPNNgG5YfPPhmXc-ItHvVUU4kRh4Cj4ePJkc1ITyGR9cuD569DJ3PDlWFig8_RghWM_CX--sDKemeyDK7EIyDQTmuLuFAK8iVKVcEd6_8xG_N165FEE_KDYcjvybV1JrAhUYdjmdau9bVazWStkVt31iIl50JgkhKjWveTImpsqaWvK_t93c7ox-6ASxuCshogjC7BghUbrPh2ccKQdgihKc20VH4CudMWpUFQ5fHC8mzYiYkJ5kEzpBFuLK2TqyLTA-z0-VfJW3o09pY34_XhcBkkZtrRzIUXRE39plsMM4uL14thNClTglOsn5psYnIlVpwkERs5vmaQkkHCpxYODtS8M462oW24Me82cLfRcAhP_gZ3cLvussIbSxtsv8iVyX3nybGE0fcUs6PEnb5VA5s5rAGi6WOXJV5BgaqHoNFrzdbRYcqsGvmss8CijV2JC8KZlx5WvIWIsltcxxvRJKPqcS8n_XZ8-PrVy-0A7kKhBuQS32UIkd2VXDEyahTupZjr-XrG4corV-4Js_hAGXuTIpt9MYtMbgVdlfjyp40cDjU3EzyhVtG2BaCmsT8_A%3D%3D)

For more than twenty years, Connecticut's 25th Senate District--representing **Norwalk** and **Darien** --has been represented by the same political leadership in Hartford. _**During that time, many residents have grown frustrated with rising costs of energy & taxes, increasing government mandates, and the feeling that their concerns are no longer being heard.**_
Now, **Justin Perry** is offering voters a different choice.
A scientist, entrepreneur, husband, and father (with another child on the way), Perry is challenging the status quo with a campaign rooted in fiscal responsibility, economic opportunity, local control, and the belief that government should serve communities--not direct them.
> "I genuinely am running to preserve the things that make this community great," Perry told supporters at his campaign kickoff. "What I've learned from so many residents is that for years they haven't felt like they had a voice representing the things they care about."
## A Different Kind of Candidate
Unlike many politicians, Perry comes from a background in medicine, science and research rather than government. He credits that experience with teaching him persistence, humility, and the importance of listening.
"As a scientist, I spend a lot of my time getting told no," Perry said. "If you get a five or ten percent success rate, you're doing very well. You learn how to keep fighting because you believe in what you're doing."
_**That perseverance, he says, is exactly what Connecticut needs.**_
Perry has built his campaign around a simple promise: he will never abandon the principles and values that brought him into the race.
_**" Fiscal responsibility, economic liberty, and the importance of community are extremely important to me,"**_ he said.
## Fighting Connecticut's Cost Crisis
One of Perry's strongest criticisms is directed at the policies that have made Connecticut increasingly expensive for families and businesses.
From some of the highest energy costs in the nation to burdensome regulations and taxes, Perry argues that state government has made it harder for residents to succeed.
_**" Why would someone want to start a business here?"**_ he asked. _**" Why would they want to invest here when energy costs are so high and the regulatory environment makes it so difficult?"**_
Having explored starting his own consulting business, Perry says he experienced firsthand the layers of permits, fees, and bureaucracy that discourage innovation and entrepreneurship.
_**" The small businesses in this district are incredible,"**_ Perry said. "I'm in awe of what they accomplish despite all the obstacles the state puts in their way."
His campaign calls for reducing unnecessary regulations, supporting job creators, and restoring Connecticut's competitiveness.
## Putting Communities Back in Charge
A recurring theme throughout Perry's campaign is the importance of local decision-making.
_He believes that too many policies are imposed from Hartford without sufficient input from the communities they affect._
Using the example of a community garden he passes regularly, Perry described how thriving communities depend on people who have invested years into building and maintaining them.
_**" The people best equipped to care for a garden are the people who have spent years tending it,"**_ he said. _**" The same is true of our towns. The people who know what is best for Norwalk and Darien are the people who live here."**_
While recognizing an important role for state government, Perry argues that Hartford should empower local communities rather than dictate to them.
## More Than a Local Race
What Justin Perry is talking about is not unique to Norwalk and Darien. His concerns mirror what residents across Connecticut have been saying for years.
For decades, Connecticut has effectively operated under one-party control in Hartford. When taxes rise, when energy costs increase, when businesses leave, when housing becomes less affordable, and when families struggle to make ends meet, voters naturally ask who is accountable for the policies that produced those outcomes.
Perry believes accountability matters.
As a scientist, he approaches problems by examining evidence, challenging assumptions, and searching for solutions rather than excuses. He believes many of Connecticut's challenges are not inevitable--they are the result of policy choices that can be changed.
In many ways, Perry represents a new generation of leadership. He brings an outsider's perspective to Hartford and a willingness to challenge a system that many residents feel has become disconnected from the people it serves.
## Republicans United Behind a New Generation of Leadership
One of the most encouraging aspects of Perry's campaign kickoff was the strong show of support from Republican leaders and candidates across the region.
It was particularly meaningful to see Gubernatorial Candidate [Ryan Fazio](https://substack.com/redirect/ed83b7b5-434a-4a85-a4b6-03872b128407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) attend the event, introduce Justin and stand alongside him.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/548d70a6-44b7-4b54-b1e0-7e25e011c4fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**Gubernatorial Candidate Ryan Fazio introducing Justin Perry**_
Ryan's presence demonstrated the importance of supporting strong down-ballot candidates and building a team that can advocate for Connecticut families at every level of government.
As the Republican endorsed candidate for US Congress (CT-04), I was honored to be invited to attend as well and show my support for Justin, talk about the intersection of local and federal issues. It was great to see a party that is united.
Too often, politics is viewed through a national lens, but real change begins locally. The decisions made in Hartford affect our taxes, our schools, our energy bills, our housing costs, and our quality of life. State elections have federal consequences, and federal policies have local impacts. Everything is connected.
That is why supporting candidates up and down the ballot matters.
_**Whether someone is running for State Senate in Norwalk and Darien, State Representative in Greenwich, Governor of Connecticut, or Congress, we all have a role to play in building a better future for our communities. And most of these candidates are talking and working together.**_
The appearance of Ryan Fazio at Perry's kickoff sent an important message: _**Republicans are working together**_. We understand that success requires building a bench of leaders who are willing to challenge the status quo and offer voters meaningful alternatives.
## A Choice for Connecticut
Justin Perry's campaign is ultimately about more than one district.
It is about whether Connecticut continues down a path of higher taxes, higher energy costs, greater government control, and declining affordability--or whether voters choose a new direction focused on accountability, opportunity, local control, and economic growth.
After more than two decades of the same representation, the people of Norwalk and Darien finally have a choice.
_**Justin Perry has my full support, and I hope he earns yours as well.**_
If Connecticut is going to move in a new direction, it will happen because citizens decide to become part of the solution rather than simply accept the status quo. Some people run for office. Others volunteer, donate, host events, knock on doors, make phone calls, or simply talk to their neighbors.
Every one of those actions matters.
To learn more about Justin Perry's campaign, volunteer, donate, or get involved, visit:
**Website:**[ justinperryforct.com](https://substack.com/redirect/ab06faea-95c4-4ffb-86a2-1f2f79d0ab31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Instagram:** @justinperryforct
This November, the voters of Norwalk and Darien will have an opportunity to make their voices heard and choose a new path forward.
The choice is theirs.

subject: Immigrant youth are the visionaries we must invest in
body:
This is a powerful reminder that immigrants are essential to building the collective future we all deserve. | | | Peter, This week, just one day after hundreds of immigrant youth and the children of immigrants mobilized to Washington, D.C., to mark the 14th anniversary of DACA, I learned that TIME named me to its inaugural Visionaries list, recognizing leaders across the country who are shaping a better future for young people. I receive this recognition with gratitude, but never alone. From student walkouts to hunger strikes,**immigrant youth have always been the visionaries taking bold action to build a future where everyone lives freely, safely, and with dignity.** **[If you believe in the power of immigrant youth to shape this country’s future, will you chip in $14 to United We Dream today—one dollar for every year of DACA?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeRSb6UyzukpYsZgexseLha1n3hAbO_p8Utnp75qrFZNpVtDR353BrPk9ZVLwmtIhTd-QhQ71BH941k-wF-CxDAl85JiFuykT5vrhWmm2O2h8uQETQyjOREvdOZtDnHylnihOTyjylJJUVoTKyUT_V0nt2QwTto-WNNtiBn2MLZvcgGXCM-jbfjcjs4YyvRdCsvs0RbjFjYDXgHtHKd6oSvUgLd3RAs-0Pw_5bFq6SLQlsYKzi6KD83ojK7AjJ0SX4aftkVsXHV16hXbxhi_4sisvA-LCFaZdbpxI_8fvBTdZYcTiPxVqpd-tfJENZ8NvVpJe32TE-lI3cnru2hPys4uY5nhXjK1ClZ_KA6fx-ZGQVP6HsYceQvrkd4IbJKLgP8GDVdorjOIN2mEE9BByjwrl7tFgKLouJ5qt3bwzKGnrCuVdwLb7OSbAu7lOIVAsK/4rl/QI_SUXPkS9CxZrpBBkXv8w/h0/h001.O_cixys7Z1YOweSAfG_yt3nDaR0OLcHEoUAEnSNKX5M)** Growing up as a young, queer immigrant in Texas, I knew what it was like to be isolated physically, politically, and economically from the fabric of our country. I joined this movement because I believed our lives mattered. Two decades later, I remain because I know immigration is one of the places our collective future will be decided. The question has never simply been about who gets to come or who gets to stay. It is: _Who gets to belong, to build wealth, and to shape our economy? Who gets to govern? Who gets to dream?_ Working people should have more power. Democracy must live in our workplaces and neighborhoods. Those who create this country’s wealth must have a voice in how it’s shared, and immigrant communities are essential to that vision. The members, organizers, and staff of United We Dream taught me that freedom is a practice. It is built whenever we organize to transform fear into power and isolation into solidarity. This recognition reflects what is possible when people decide they are worthy of governing the future they envision. **[Courage is collective, hope is disciplined, and the future is built by people like you and the 1.2 million members of United We Dream who refuse to live in the shadows. clean_body: This is a powerful reminder that immigrants are essential to building the collective future we all deserve. | | | Peter, This week, just one day after hundreds of immigrant youth and the children of immigrants mobilized to Washington, D.C., to mark the 14th anniversary of DACA, I learned that TIME named me to its inaugural Visionaries list, recognizing leaders across the country who are shaping a better future for young people. I receive this recognition with gratitude, but never alone. From student walkouts to hunger strikes,immigrant youth have always been the visionaries taking bold action to build a future where everyone lives freely, safely, and with dignity. Growing up as a young, queer immigrant in Texas, I knew what it was like to be isolated physically, politically, and economically from the fabric of our country. I joined this movement because I believed our lives mattered. Two decades later, I remain because I know immigration is one of the places our collective future will be decided. The question has never simply been about who gets to come or who gets to stay. It is: Who gets to belong, to build wealth, and to shape our economy? Who gets to govern? Who gets to dream? Working people should have more power. Democracy must live in our workplaces and neighborhoods. Those who create this country’s wealth must have a voice in how it’s shared, and immigrant communities are essential to that vision. The members, organizers, and staff of United We Dream taught me that freedom is a practice. It is built whenever we organize to transform fear into power and isolation into solidarity. This recognition reflects what is possible when people decide they are worthy of governing the future they envision.
